title.zh: 卷15 志第10 音樂下
title.raw: 卷15 志第10 音樂下 Volume 15 Treatises 10: Music 3

sentences.zh: 開皇九年，平陳，獲宋、齊舊樂，詔于太常置清商署以管之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, after the conquest of Chen, the court acquired the old music of Song and Qi; an edict ordered the establishment of a Qing Shang Office under the Director of Ceremonies to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 9, after Chen fell, Song and Qi court music was seized and a Qing Shang Office was set up under the Grand Music Master.

sentences.zh: 求陳太樂令蔡子元、於普明等，復居其職。

translations.literal: Chen's former Director of Music Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and others were sought out and restored to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and other former Chen music officials were found and reappointed.

sentences.zh: 由是牛弘奏曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon Niu Hong memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong then submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞周有六代之樂，至《韶》、《武》而已。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Zhou possessed the music of six dynasties, extending only as far as the Shao and the Wu.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Zhou kept the music of six ages, down only to the Shao and the Wu.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇改周舞曰《五行》，漢高帝改《韶舞》曰《文始》，以示不相襲也。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin changed the Zhou dance to the Five Elements; Emperor Gaozu of Han changed the Shao Dance to the Wen Shi, to show that one did not simply inherit the previous dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang renamed the Zhou dance Five Elements; Han Gaozu renamed the Shao Dance Wen Shi—to mark a break with the past.

sentences.zh: 又造《武德》，自表其功，故高帝廟奏《武德》、《文始》、《五行》之舞。

translations.literal: He also created the Martial Virtue, proclaiming his own achievements; hence at Gaozu's temple the dances Martial Virtue, Wen Shi, and Five Elements were performed.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed Martial Virtue to celebrate his own deeds, so Gaozu's temple used the Martial Virtue, Wen Shi, and Five Elements dances.

sentences.zh: 又作《昭容》、《禮容》，增演其意。

translations.literal: He further composed Bright Countenance and Ritual Countenance, expanding and elaborating their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He also added Bright Countenance and Ritual Countenance, developing their themes further.

sentences.zh: 《昭容》生於《武德》，蓋猶古之《韶》也。

translations.literal: Bright Countenance arose from Martial Virtue—it was essentially the ancient Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Countenance grew out of Martial Virtue and was in effect the old Shao.

sentences.zh: 《禮容》生於《文始》，矯秦之《五行》也。

translations.literal: Ritual Countenance arose from Wen Shi, correcting Qin's Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual Countenance grew out of Wen Shi, correcting Qin's Five Elements dance.

sentences.zh: 文帝又作《四時》之舞，故孝景帝立，追述先功，采《武德舞》作《昭德舞》，被之管弦，薦于太宗之廟。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen also composed the Four Seasons dance; thus when Emperor Xiaojing acceded, tracing the achievements of his predecessors, he took the Martial Virtue Dance to make the Bright Virtue Dance, set it to strings and pipes, and offered it at the temple of the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen added a Four Seasons dance; Xiaojing later drew on Martial Virtue to create Bright Virtue, scored it for orchestra, and presented it at the Founding Emperor's temple.

sentences.zh: 孝宣采《昭德舞》為《盛德舞》，更造新歌，薦于武帝之廟。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoxuan took the Bright Virtue Dance and made it the Flourishing Virtue Dance, composing new songs and offering them at Emperor Wu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxuan reworked Bright Virtue into Flourishing Virtue with new lyrics for Emperor Wu's temple.

sentences.zh: 據此而言，遞相因襲，縱有改作，並宗於《韶》。

translations.literal: Judging from this, each generation inherited the last; even when new works were made, all traced back to the Shao.
translations.idiomatic: On this evidence, titles changed but the line always led back to the Shao.

sentences.zh: 至明帝時，東平獻王采《文德舞》為《大武》之舞，薦于光武之廟。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Ming, the Prince of Dongping took the Cultured Virtue Dance and made it the Great Martial dance, offering it at Emperor Guangwu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming, the Prince of Dongping turned Cultured Virtue into the Great Martial dance for Guangwu's temple.

sentences.zh: 漢末大亂，樂章淪缺，魏武平荊州，獲杜夔，以為軍謀祭酒，使創雅樂。

translations.literal: At the end of Han came great disorder and the ritual scores were lost; when Wei Wu conquered Jing province he obtained Du Kui, made him Army Planning Libationer, and had him create court ritual music.
translations.idiomatic: Han collapsed into chaos and the scores vanished; Cao Cao captured Du Kui in Jingzhou, made him Army Planning Libationer, and charged him with restoring court music.

sentences.zh: 時散騎侍郎鄧靜善詠雅歌，樂師尹胡能習宗祀之曲，舞師馮肅曉知先代諸舞。

translations.literal: At the time, Palace Attendant Deng Jing was skilled at singing ritual songs; music master Yin Hu knew the ancestral-sacrifice pieces; dance master Feng Su understood the dances of earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jing could sing the ritual songs, Yin Hu knew the sacrificial repertoire, and Feng Su knew the old dances.

sentences.zh: 總練研精，復于古樂，自夔始也。

translations.literal: Gathering their training and refining it with care, they restored the ancient music—beginning with Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Pooling their expertise, they restored ancient music—starting with Kui.

sentences.zh: 文帝黃初，改《昭容》之樂為《昭業樂》，《武德》之舞為《武頌舞》，《文始》之舞為《大韶舞》，《五行》之舞為《大武舞》。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era of Emperor Wen, the music Bright Countenance was changed to Bright Achievement Music; the Martial Virtue dance to Martial Hymn Dance; the Wen Shi dance to Great Shao Dance; and the Five Elements dance to Great Martial Dance.
translations.idiomatic: In Wen's Huangchu reign, Bright Countenance became Bright Achievement, Martial Virtue became Martial Hymn, Wen Shi became Great Shao, and Five Elements became Great Martial.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，公卿奏上太祖武皇帝樂曰《武始》之舞，高祖文皇帝樂曰《咸熙》之舞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, the high officials submitted that the music of Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu should be the Martial Beginning dance, and that of High Ancestor Emperor Wen the Xianxi dance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Ming's reign, officials proposed Martial Beginning for Cao Cao and Xianxi for Cao Pi.

sentences.zh: 又制樂舞，名曰《章斌》之舞，有事於天地宗廟及臨朝大饗，並用之。

translations.literal: He also regulated a music-dance called the Zhang Bin dance, used together for rites to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples, and for grand feasts at court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He also instituted the Zhang Bin dance for Heaven-and-Earth and temple rites and for great court banquets.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始二年，遣傅玄等造行禮及上壽食舉歌詩。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, Fu Xuan and others were dispatched to compose songs for processional rites, longevity toasts, and banquet music.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taishi 2, Fu Xuan and others were sent to write processional, longevity, and banquet songs.

sentences.zh: 張華表曰：「按漢、魏所用，雖詩章辭異，興廢隨時，至其韻逗曲折，並系於舊，一皆因襲，不敢有所改也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua memorialized: "Examining what Han and Wei used, although the texts of the poems differ and pieces rose and fell with the times, their cadences and turns all depend on the old models—every one was inherited, and none dared to be altered."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua wrote: "Han and Wei pieces differ in wording and came and went with the times, but their phrasing and turns all followed old models—nothing was boldly changed."

sentences.zh: 」九年，荀勖典樂，使郭夏、宋識造《正德》、《大豫》之舞。

translations.literal: "In the ninth year, Xun Xu oversaw music and had Guo Xia and Song Shi create the Correct Virtue and Great Yu dances."
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, Xun Xu had Guo Xia and Song Shi compose Correct Virtue and Great Yu.

sentences.zh: 改魏《昭武舞》曰《宣武舞》，羽籥舞曰《宜文舞》。

translations.literal: The Wei Bright Martial Dance was changed to the Propagating Martial Dance, and the feather-and-flute dance to the Propagating Culture Dance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Bright Martial became Propagating Martial, and the feather-flute dance became Propagating Culture.

sentences.zh: 江左之初，典章堙紊，賀循為太常卿，始有登歌之樂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Eastern Jin, statutes were buried in disorder; when He Xun became Director of Ceremonies, there were at last songs for the ascent hymn.
translations.idiomatic: Early Eastern Jin law was in disarray; under He Xun as Grand Music Master, ascent hymns finally appeared.

sentences.zh: 大寧末，阮孚等又增益之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daning era, Ruan Fu and others added to them further.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daning, Ruan Fu and others expanded the repertoire.

sentences.zh: 咸和間，鳩集遺逸，鄴沒胡後，樂人頗復南度，東晉因之，以具鐘律。

translations.literal: During the Xianhe period, scattered survivors were gathered; after Ye fell to the barbarians, many musicians crossed south again, and Eastern Jin thereby acquired bells and pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianhe, refugees were collected; after Ye fell, musicians fled south and Eastern Jin finally had bells and pipes.

sentences.zh: 太元間，破苻永固，又獲樂工楊蜀等，閑練舊樂，於是金石始備。

translations.literal: During the Taiyuan period, after the defeat of Fu Yonggu, the musicians Yang Shu and others were also captured; versed in the old music, they at last completed the full ensemble of metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan, after Fu Yonggu was beaten, musicians like Yang Shu restored the old repertoire and metal-and-stone instruments were complete.

sentences.zh: 尋其設懸音調，並與江左是同。

translations.literal: Examining their suspended-instrument pitch systems, they were the same as those of the Eastern Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Their pitch arrangements matched those of the Eastern Jin.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂破慕容永于長子，盡獲苻氏舊樂。

translations.literal: Murong Chui defeated Murong Yong at Changzi and seized all the old music of the Fu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui beat Murong Yong at Changzi and took the Fu dynasty's entire musical legacy.

sentences.zh: 垂息為魏所敗，其鐘律令李佛等，將太樂細伎，奔慕容德於鄴。

translations.literal: When Chui's son Xi was defeated by Wei, the bell-and-pitch director Li Fo and others took the finest performers of the Grand Music Office and fled to Murong De at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: After Chui's son Xi lost to Wei, pitch-master Li Fo fled to Murong De at Ye with the Grand Music performers.

sentences.zh: 德遷都廣固，子超嗣立，其母先沒姚興，超乙太樂伎一百二十人詣興贖母。

translations.literal: De moved the capital to Guanggu; when his son Chao succeeded, Chao's mother had earlier been captured by Yao Xing, and Chao sent one hundred twenty Grand Music performers to Xing to ransom her.
translations.idiomatic: De moved to Guanggu; when Chao succeeded, he sent 120 musicians to Yao Xing to ransom his captive mother.

sentences.zh: 及宋武帝入關，悉收南渡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song entered the passes, all who had fled south were collected.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu entered the passes, every southern refugee musician was gathered in.

sentences.zh: 永初元年，改《正德舞》曰《前舞》，《大武舞》曰《後舞》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu, the Correct Virtue Dance was renamed the Front Dance, and the Great Martial Dance the Rear Dance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 1, Correct Virtue became the Front Dance and Great Martial the Rear Dance.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉九年，太樂令鐘宗之，更調金石。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, the Director of Music Zhong Zongzhi retuned the bells and stones.
translations.idiomatic: In Wen's Yuanjia 9, Music Director Zhong Zongzhi retuned bells and stones.

sentences.zh: 至十四年，典書令奚縱，復改定之。

translations.literal: By the fourteenth year, the Director of Documents Xi Zong revised and fixed them again.
translations.idiomatic: By year 14, Documents Director Xi Zong had revised them again.

sentences.zh: 又有《凱容》、《宣業》之舞，齊代因而用之。

translations.literal: There were also the Triumphal Countenance and Propagating Achievement dances, which Qi continued to use.
translations.idiomatic: Qi also kept the Triumphal Countenance and Propagating Achievement dances.

sentences.zh: 蕭子顯《齊書·志》曰：「宋孝建初，朝議以《凱容舞》為《韶舞》，《宣業舞》為《武德舞》。

translations.literal: Xiao Zixian's "Treatise" in the Book of Qi says: "At the beginning of Xiaojian in Song, court discussion took the Triumphal Countenance Dance as the Shao Dance and the Propagating Achievement Dance as the Martial Virtue Dance."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zixian's Qi Treatise notes that in Song's Xiaojian era, court debate equated Triumphal Countenance with Shao and Propagating Achievement with Martial Virtue.

sentences.zh: 據《韶》為言，《宣業》即是古之《大武》，非《武德》也。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of the Shao, Propagating Achievement is the ancient Great Martial—not Martial Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: By Shao standards, Propagating Achievement is the old Great Martial, not Martial Virtue.

sentences.zh: 」故《志》有《前舞凱容》歌辭，《後舞凱容》歌辭者矣。

translations.literal: "Hence the Treatise contains the lyrics for the Front-Dance Triumphal Countenance and the Rear-Dance Triumphal Countenance."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Treatise preserves lyrics for Front and Rear Triumphal Countenance.

sentences.zh: 至於梁初，猶用《凱容》、《宣業》之舞，後改為《大壯》、《大觀》焉。

translations.literal: In the early Liang they still used the Triumphal Countenance and Propagating Achievement dances; later these were changed to Great Strength and Great Vision.
translations.idiomatic: Early Liang kept Triumphal Countenance and Propagating Achievement; later they became Great Strength and Great Vision.

sentences.zh: 今人猶喚《大觀》為《前舞》，故知樂名雖隨代而改，聲韻曲折，理應常同。

translations.literal: People today still call Great Vision the Front Dance; thus although music names change with each dynasty, the turns of sound and tone ought to remain the same.
translations.idiomatic: Great Vision is still called the Front Dance today—titles change by dynasty, but the melodic turns should stay the same.

sentences.zh: 前克荊州，得梁家雅曲，今平蔣州，又得陳氏正樂。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jing province was taken, the elegant pieces of the Liang house were obtained; now, with the pacification of Jiang province, the orthodox music of the Chen house has also been acquired.
translations.idiomatic: We already took Liang's elegant repertoire with Jingzhou; pacifying Jiangzhou has now brought Chen's orthodox music as well.

sentences.zh: 史傳相承，以為合古。

translations.literal: Historical tradition hands this down as matching antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Historians treat this succession as genuinely ancient.

sentences.zh: 且觀其曲體，用聲有次，請修緝之，以備雅樂。

translations.literal: Moreover, examining the structure of the pieces, the use of tones is ordered; please edit and compile them to complete the court ritual repertoire.
translations.idiomatic: Their forms are ordered and their tones sequenced—please edit them into proper court ritual music.

sentences.zh: 其後魏洛陽之曲，據《魏史》云「太武平赫連昌所得」，更無明證。

translations.literal: As for the later Wei music of Luoyang, the Wei History says only that it was "obtained when Emperor Taiwu conquered Helian Chang"—there is no further clear evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Luoyang pieces are attested only by the Wei History's note on Taiwu's capture of Helian Chang—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 後周所用者，皆是新造，雜有邊裔之聲。

translations.literal: What Later Zhou used was all newly made, mixed with sounds from the frontier regions.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou used newly composed music laced with frontier sounds.

sentences.zh: 戎音亂華，皆不可用。

translations.literal: Barbarian tones disorder Chinese music—none may be used.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian tones corrupt Chinese music and must not be used.

sentences.zh: 請悉停之。

translations.literal: Please stop them all.
translations.idiomatic: Please suspend all of them.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「制禮作樂，聖人之事也，功成化洽，方可議之。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Regulating rites and making music are the affairs of sages; only when achievement is complete and transformation fully harmonized may one discuss them."
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Rites and music belong to sages—only after triumph and full civil harmony may they be reworked."

sentences.zh: 今宇內初平，正化未洽。

translations.literal: Now the realm has only just been pacified and proper transformation is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is barely pacified and proper civilization not yet settled.

sentences.zh: 遽有變革，我則未暇。

translations.literal: To rush into change—I have no leisure for that.
translations.idiomatic: I have no time for sudden change.

sentences.zh: 」晉王廣又表請，帝乃許之。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang again memorialized requesting permission, and the Emperor then assented.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yang Guang petitioned again, and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 牛弘遂因鄭譯之舊，又請依古五聲六律，旋相為宮。

translations.literal: Niu Hong then, following Zheng Yi's earlier work, also requested that the ancient five tones and six pitch-pipes be used, cyclically modulating as palace keys.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong, building on Zheng Yi, also asked to restore cyclical palace modulation from the five tones and six pitch-pipes.

sentences.zh: 雅樂每宮但一調，唯迎氣奏五調，謂之五音。

translations.literal: In court ritual music each palace key had only one mode; only for welcoming the qi were five modes played—these were called the five tones.
translations.idiomatic: Court music used one mode per palace key; only qi-welcoming rites used five modes—the five tones.

sentences.zh: 縵樂用七調，祭祀施用。

translations.literal: Slow music used seven modes and was employed in sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Slow ceremonial music used seven modes for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 各依聲律尊卑為次。

translations.literal: Each was ordered according to the rank of pitch and tone.
translations.idiomatic: Each was ranked by pitch hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 高祖猶憶妥言，注弘奏下，不許作旋宮之樂，但作黃鐘一宮而已。

translations.literal: Gaozu still remembered Tuo's words; he annotated Niu Hong's memorial and rejected cyclical-palace music, allowing only a single Yellow Bell palace key.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heeded Tuo's advice, annotated Niu Hong's memorial, and forbade cyclical modulation—only Yellow Bell palace would do.

sentences.zh: 於是牛弘及秘書丞姚察、通直散騎常侍許善心、儀同三司劉臻、通直郎虞世基等，更共詳議曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon Niu Hong, Secretariat Aide Yao Cha, Palace Attendant Xu Shanxin, Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes Liu Zhen, and Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shiji and others jointly deliberated further, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong, Yao Cha, Xu Shanxin, Liu Zhen, Yu Shiji, and others then deliberated jointly:

sentences.zh: 後周之時，以四聲降神，雖采《周禮》，而年代深遠，其法久絕，不可依用。

translations.literal: In Later Zhou, four tones were used to summon the spirits; although this drew on the Rites of Zhou, the age was remote and the method long extinct—it cannot be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou's four-tone spirit-summoning rite cited the Rites of Zhou, but the method was long dead and unusable.

sentences.zh: 謹案《司樂》：「凡樂，圜鐘為宮，黃鐘為角，太簇為徵，姑洗為羽，舞《雲門》以祭天。

translations.literal: We respectfully examine the Director of Music: "For all music: with Round Bell as palace, Yellow Bell as horn, Great Cluster as bell-note, and Maiden Wash as feather, perform the Cloud Gate dance to sacrifice to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Music states: "For Heaven: Round Bell palace, Yellow Bell horn, Great Cluster bell-note, Maiden Wash feather—dance Cloud Gate."

sentences.zh: 函鐘為宮，太簇為角，姑洗為徵，南呂為羽，舞《咸池》以祭地。

translations.literal: With Enclosing Bell as palace, Great Cluster as horn, Maiden Wash as bell-note, and Southern Pitch as feather, perform the Xian Chi dance to sacrifice to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: For Earth: Enclosing Bell palace, Great Cluster horn, Maiden Wash bell-note, Southern Pitch feather—dance Xian Chi.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘為宮，大呂為角，太簇為徵，圜鐘為羽，舞《韻》以祀宗廟。

translations.literal: With Yellow Bell as palace, Great Pitch as horn, Great Cluster as bell-note, and Round Bell as feather, perform the Great Martial dance to sacrifice at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: For the ancestral temple: Yellow Bell palace, Great Pitch horn, Great Cluster bell-note, Round Bell feather—dance Great Martial.

sentences.zh: 」馬融曰：「圜鐘，應鐘也。

translations.literal: Ma Rong said: "Round Bell is Responding Bell."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong identified Round Bell with Responding Bell.

sentences.zh: 」賈逵、鄭玄曰：「圜鐘，夾鐘也。

translations.literal: Jia Kui and Zheng Xuan said: "Round Bell is Pinched Bell."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui and Zheng Xuan took Round Bell to mean Pinched Bell.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄又云：「此樂無商聲，祭尚柔剛，故不用也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan also said: "This music has no commercial tone; sacrifice honors soft and hard, hence it is not used."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan added that this music omits the commercial tone because sacrifice balances firmness and yielding.

sentences.zh: 」干寶云：「不言商，商為臣。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "Commercial is not mentioned because commercial is the minister."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said commercial is unnamed because it represents the minister.

sentences.zh: 王者自謂，故置其實而去其名，若曰有天地人物，無德以主之，謙以自牧也。

translations.literal: The king speaks for himself, so he keeps the substance and removes the name—as if to say there are Heaven, Earth, and the people, yet no virtue to rule them; humility in self-governance.
translations.idiomatic: The king keeps the substance but drops the name—humility before Heaven, Earth, and the people.

sentences.zh: 」先儒解釋，既莫知適從。

translations.literal: The explanations of earlier scholars leave one with no clear guide.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier commentators disagree, leaving no clear authority.

sentences.zh: 然此四聲，非直無商，又律管乖次，以其為樂，無克諧之理。

translations.literal: Yet these four tones not only lack commercial outright—the pitch pipes are out of sequence; used as music, they cannot achieve harmony.
translations.idiomatic: These four tones lack commercial and mis-order the pipes—they cannot harmonize as music.

sentences.zh: 今古事異，不可得而行也。

translations.literal: Ancient and modern circumstances differ; this cannot be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Times have changed; the scheme cannot be enacted.

sentences.zh: 按《東觀書·馬防傳》，太子丞鮑鄴等上作樂事，下防。

translations.literal: According to the Biography of Ma Fang in the Eastern View Annals, Palace Aide Bao Ye and others submitted a proposal on making music, which was sent down to Fang.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern View Annals record that Bao Ye and others submitted a music proposal to Ma Fang.

sentences.zh: 防奏言：「建初二年七月鄴上言，天子食飲，必順於四時五味，而有食舉之樂。

translations.literal: Fang memorialized: "In the seventh month of the second year of Jianchu, Ye reported that the Son of Heaven's food and drink must follow the four seasons and five flavors, and that there is music for raising the dishes."
translations.idiomatic: Fang wrote: "In Jianchu 2, month 7, Ye reported that royal meals follow season and flavor and require dish-raising music."

sentences.zh: 所以順天地，養神明，求福應也。

translations.literal: This is to accord with Heaven and Earth, nourish the spirits, and seek responsive blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Such music aligns Heaven and Earth, nourishes the spirits, and seeks blessing.

sentences.zh: 今官雅樂獨有黃鐘，而食舉樂但有太簇，皆不應月律，恐傷氣類。

translations.literal: Now official court music has only Yellow Bell, while dish-raising music has only Great Cluster—neither matches the monthly pitch pipes, and qi may be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Court music uses only Yellow Bell and dish music only Great Cluster—neither follows monthly pipes and may disturb the qi.

sentences.zh: 可作十二月均，各應其月氣。

translations.literal: Twelve monthly modes may be made, each matching its month's qi.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve monthly modes could match each month's qi.

sentences.zh: 公卿朝會，得聞月律，乃能感天，和氣宜應。

translations.literal: When the high officials assemble at court and hear the monthly pitch pipes, they can move Heaven and harmonious qi should respond.
translations.idiomatic: If officials heard the monthly pipes at court, Heaven would be moved and harmonious qi would answer.

sentences.zh: 詔下太常評焉。

translations.literal: An edict was sent down to the Director of Ceremonies for evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Grand Music Master.

sentences.zh: 太常上言，作樂器直錢百四十六萬，奏寢。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonies reported that making the instruments would cost 1,460,000 cash; the memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Music Master priced instruments at 1,460,000 cash; the proposal died.

sentences.zh: 今明詔復下，臣防以為可須上天之明時，因歲首之嘉月，發太簇之律，奏雅頌之音，以迎和氣。

translations.literal: Now a clear edict has come down again; your subject Fang believes one may await Heaven's bright season, take advantage of the auspicious month at the year's start, sound the Great Cluster pitch pipe, and perform the elegant and hymn texts to welcome harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Fang now urged using the year's first auspicious month to sound Great Cluster and perform elegant hymns to welcome harmonious qi.

sentences.zh: 」其條貫甚具，遂獨施行。

translations.literal: "The provisions were very detailed, and this alone was put into practice."
translations.idiomatic: The plan was detailed and this measure alone was adopted.

sentences.zh: 起於十月，為迎氣之樂矣。

translations.literal: Beginning in the tenth month, it became the music for welcoming the qi.
translations.idiomatic: From the tenth month onward it served as qi-welcoming music.

sentences.zh: 又《順帝紀》云：「陽嘉二年冬十月庚午，以春秋為辟雍，隸太學，隨月律。

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Shun also say: "In the tenth month of the second year of Yangjia, winter, day gengwu, the spring-and-autumn sacrifice became the Bright Enclosure, subordinate to the Imperial Academy, following the monthly pitch pipes."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun's annals note that in Yangjia 2, month 10, gengwu, the Bright Enclosure rite followed monthly pipes under the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 十月作應鐘，三月作姑洗。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Responding Bell was made; in the third month Maiden Wash.
translations.idiomatic: Responding Bell was tuned in month 10; Maiden Wash in month 3.

sentences.zh: 元和以來，音戾不調，修復黃鐘，作樂器，如舊典。

translations.literal: Since the Yuanhe era, pitches had been discordant; Yellow Bell was restored and instruments made according to the old canon.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuanhe pitches had drifted; Yellow Bell was restored and instruments rebuilt to the old standard.

sentences.zh: 」據此而言，漢樂宮懸有黃鐘均，食舉太簇均，止有二均，不旋相為宮，亦以明矣。

translations.literal: Judging from this, Han music's suspended ensemble had a Yellow Bell mode and dish-raising a Great Cluster mode—only these two modes, not cyclical palace modulation, is likewise clear.
translations.idiomatic: Han court music had only Yellow Bell and Great Cluster modes—two modes, not cyclical modulation.

sentences.zh: 計從元和至陽嘉二年，才五十歲，用而復止。

translations.literal: From Yuanhe to the second year of Yangjia was only fifty years—used and then stopped again.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanhe to Yangjia 2 was only fifty years—adopted, then abandoned.

sentences.zh: 驗黃帝聽鳳以制律呂，《尚書》曰「予欲聞六律五聲」，《周禮》有「分樂而祭」。

translations.literal: Verify that the Yellow Emperor listened to the phoenix to set the pitch pipes and tones; the Book of Documents says "I wish to hear the six pitch pipes and five tones"; the Rites of Zhou have "assign music and sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor heard the phoenix to fix pipes and tones; the Documents say "I wish to hear six pipes and five tones"; the Rites of Zhou assign music to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 此聖人製作，以合天地陰陽之和，自然之理，乃雲音戾不調，斯言誣之甚也。

translations.literal: These are creations of sages, made to match the harmony of Heaven and Earth, yin and yang—the natural principle; to say pitches were discordant is gross slander.
translations.idiomatic: Sages fashioned music to match cosmic harmony—calling the pipes "discordant" is slander.

sentences.zh: 今梁、陳雅曲，並用宮聲。

translations.literal: Now the elegant pieces of Liang and Chen all use the palace tone.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Chen elegant pieces all use palace tone.

sentences.zh: 按《禮》：「五聲十二律，還相為宮。

translations.literal: According to the Rites: "The five tones and twelve pitch pipes cyclically serve as palace keys."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: "Five tones and twelve pipes cyclically form palace keys."

sentences.zh: 」盧植云：「十二月三管流轉用事，當用事者為宮。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi said: "Through the twelve months three pipes rotate in office; whichever is in office serves as palace."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi explained that whichever monthly pipe is "in office" becomes palace.

sentences.zh: 宮，君也。

translations.literal: Palace means ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Palace means "ruler."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄曰：「五聲宮、商、角、徵、羽。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "The five tones are palace, commercial, horn, bell-note, and feather."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan named the five tones: palace, commercial, horn, bell-note, and feather.

sentences.zh: 其陽管為律，陰管為呂。

translations.literal: The yang pipes are pitch pipes; the yin pipes are pitch tubes.
translations.idiomatic: Yang pipes are pitch pipes; yin pipes are pitch tubes.

sentences.zh: 布十二辰，更相為宮，始自黃鐘，終於南呂，凡六十也。

translations.literal: Spread across the twelve branches, each in turn serves as palace, beginning with Yellow Bell and ending with Southern Pitch—sixty in all.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve branches rotate as palace from Yellow Bell to Southern Pitch—sixty combinations in all.

sentences.zh: 」皇侃疏：「還相為宮者，十一月以黃鐘為宮，十二月以大呂為宮，正月乙太簇為宮。

translations.literal: Huang Kan's commentary: "Cyclically serving as palace means: in the eleventh month Yellow Bell is palace, in the twelfth month Great Pitch is palace, in the first month Great Cluster is palace."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kan glossed cyclical palace: month 11 Yellow Bell, month 12 Great Pitch, month 1 Great Cluster.

sentences.zh: 餘月放此。

translations.literal: The remaining months follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Other months follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 凡十二管，各備五聲，合六十聲。

translations.literal: All twelve pipes each possess the five tones, totaling sixty tones.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pipes each carry five tones—sixty tones total.

sentences.zh: 五聲成一調，故十二調。

translations.literal: Five tones form one mode; hence twelve modes.
translations.idiomatic: Five tones make one mode, hence twelve modes.

sentences.zh: 」此即釋鄭義之明文，無用商、角、徵、羽為別調之法矣。

translations.literal: "This is the explicit text explaining Zheng's meaning; there is no method of using commercial, horn, bell-note, and feather as separate modes."
translations.idiomatic: This explicitly explains Zheng's view—commercial, horn, bell-note, and feather are not separate modes.

sentences.zh: 《樂稽耀嘉》曰：「東方春，其聲角，樂當宮于夾鐘。

translations.literal: The Music Appraisal and Auspicious Omen says: "In the east, spring—its tone is horn; music should take palace in Pinched Bell."
translations.idiomatic: The Music Appraisal says: in eastern spring the horn tone should take palace in Pinched Bell.

sentences.zh: 餘方各以其中律為宮。

translations.literal: Each direction likewise takes the central pitch pipe of its region as palace.
translations.idiomatic: Each direction uses its central pitch pipe as palace.

sentences.zh: 」若有商、角之理，不得雲宮于夾鐘也。

translations.literal: If there were a logic of commercial and horn tones, one could not say "palace in Pinched Bell."
translations.idiomatic: If commercial and horn were separate modes, "palace in Pinched Bell" would be impossible.

sentences.zh: 又云：「五音非宮不調，五味非甘不和。

translations.literal: It also says: "Of the five tones, none is harmonious without palace; of the five flavors, none blends without sweetness."
translations.idiomatic: It adds: no tone harmonizes without palace; no flavor blends without sweetness.

sentences.zh: 」又《動聲儀》：「宮唱而商和，是謂善本，太平之樂也。

translations.literal: The Moving Sound Instrument says: "Palace sings and commercial responds—this is called a sound foundation, the music of great peace."
translations.idiomatic: The Moving Sound Instrument: palace leads and commercial answers—the music of great peace.

sentences.zh: 」《周禮》：「奏黃鐘，歌大呂，以祀天神。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: "Play Yellow Bell, sing Great Pitch, to sacrifice to the Heavenly Spirit."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou: play Yellow Bell, sing Great Pitch, for the Heavenly Spirit.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄「以黃鐘之鐘，大呂之聲為均。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan: "With the bell of Yellow Bell and the sound of Great Pitch as the mode."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glossed this as Yellow Bell bells and Great Pitch voice forming the mode.

sentences.zh: 」均，調也。

translations.literal: Mode means tuning.
translations.idiomatic: Mode means tuning.

sentences.zh: 故崔靈恩云：「六樂十二調，亦不獨論商、角、徵、羽也。

translations.literal: Hence Cui Ling'en said: "The six ritual musics and twelve modes likewise do not treat commercial, horn, bell-note, and feather separately."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ling'en held that the six ritual musics and twelve modes never treat commercial, horn, bell-note, and feather as separate modes.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「凡六樂者，皆文之以五聲，播之以八音。

translations.literal: He also said: "For all six ritual musics, ornament them with the five tones and spread them with the eight sounds."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: all six ritual musics are ornamented with five tones and spread with eight sounds.

sentences.zh: 」故知每曲皆須五聲八音錯綜而能成也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows each piece must interweave five tones and eight sounds to be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Each piece must interweave five tones and eight sounds to be complete.

sentences.zh: 《禦寇子》云：「師文鼓琴，命宮而總四聲，則慶雲浮，景風翔。

translations.literal: The Master of Yu said: "Shi Wen played the zither; commanding palace he gathered the four tones, then auspicious clouds floated and the bright wind soared."
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Yu records that Shi Wen, commanding palace and gathering four tones, made auspicious clouds rise and the bright wind soar.

sentences.zh: 」唯《韓詩》云：「聞其宮聲，使人溫厚而寬大。

translations.literal: Only the Han Poetry says: "Hearing its palace tone makes one warm, generous, and broad."
translations.idiomatic: Han Poetry alone says palace tone makes one warm, generous, and broad.

sentences.zh: 聞其商聲，使人方廉而好義。

translations.literal: Hearing its commercial tone makes one upright, incorruptible, and devoted to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Commercial tone makes one upright, incorruptible, and devoted to righteousness.

sentences.zh: 」及古有清角、清征之流。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were also the Clear Horn and Clear Bell-note types.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity also knew Clear Horn and Clear Bell-note pieces.

sentences.zh: 此則當聲為曲。

translations.literal: These take a single tone as the piece.
translations.idiomatic: These treat a single tone as the whole piece.

sentences.zh: 今以五引為五聲，迎氣所用者是也。

translations.literal: Now the five introductory pieces serve as the five tones—these are what qi-welcoming rites use.
translations.idiomatic: The five introductory pieces now serve as the five tones for qi-welcoming rites.

sentences.zh: 餘曲悉用宮聲，不勞商、角、徵、羽。

translations.literal: All other pieces use palace tone; commercial, horn, bell-note, and feather need not be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Other pieces all use palace tone without separate commercial, horn, bell-note, or feather modes.

sentences.zh: 何以得知？

translations.literal: How may one know this?
translations.idiomatic: How do we know?

sentences.zh: 荀勖論三調為均首者，得正聲之名，明知雅樂悉在宮調。

translations.literal: When Xun Xu discussed the three modes as mode-heads, he obtained the name of orthodox tone—clearly knowing that court ritual music all lies in palace mode.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu's three mode-heads prove court ritual music belongs to palace mode.

sentences.zh: 已外徵、羽、角，自為謠俗之音耳。

translations.literal: Beyond that, bell-note, feather, and horn are merely popular folk tones.
translations.idiomatic: Bell-note, feather, and horn beyond that are merely folk tones.

sentences.zh: 且西涼、龜茲雜伎等，曲數既多，故得隸於眾調，調各別曲，至如雅樂少，須以宮為本，曆十二均而作，不可分配餘調，更成雜亂也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Western Liang, Kucha, and mixed variety pieces are numerous and can be assigned to many modes, each mode with its own piece; but court ritual music is few and must take palace as foundation, made across twelve modes—it cannot be divided among other modes without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier variety pieces fill many modes, but court music is sparse and must be built on palace across twelve modes.

sentences.zh: 其奏大抵如此。

translations.literal: The performance was broadly as described.
translations.idiomatic: Performance followed this scheme broadly.

sentences.zh: 帝並從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 故隋代雅樂，唯奏黃鐘一宮，郊廟饗用一調，迎氣用五調。

translations.literal: Thus Sui court ritual music played only the Yellow Bell palace key; suburban and temple feasts used one mode; qi-welcoming used five modes.
translations.idiomatic: Sui court music used only Yellow Bell palace; suburban feasts one mode; qi-welcoming five modes.

sentences.zh: 舊工更盡，其餘聲律，皆不復通。

translations.literal: The old masters were gradually exhausted; the remaining pitch laws were no longer understood.
translations.idiomatic: Old masters died out and the remaining pitch laws were lost.

sentences.zh: 或有能為蕤賓之宮者，享祀之際肆之，竟無覺者。

translations.literal: Some could perform in Flourishing Guest palace; during sacrifices it was played at will, yet no one noticed.
translations.idiomatic: Some could play Flourishing Guest palace at sacrifices unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 弘又修皇后房內之樂，據毛萇、侯苞、孫毓故事，皆有鐘聲，而王肅之意，乃言不可。

translations.literal: Hong also revised the inner-chamber music of the empress, following the precedents of Mao Chang, Hou Bao, and Sun Yu—all had bell sounds; but Wang Su held this impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Hong also revised empress inner-chamber music; Wang Su argued against bells despite earlier precedents.

sentences.zh: 又陳統云：「婦人無外事，而陰教尚柔，柔以靜為體，不宜用於鐘。

translations.literal: Chen Tong also said: "Women have no external affairs; yin teaching honors yielding, and yielding takes stillness as its substance—bells are unsuitable."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tong said women's teaching honors yielding stillness—bells are unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 」弘等采肅、統以取正焉。

translations.literal: Hong and others adopted Su and Tong to establish the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Hong followed Su and Tong.

sentences.zh: 高祖龍潛時，頗好音樂，常倚琵琶，作歌二首，名曰《地厚》、《天高》，托言夫妻之義。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was still rising, he greatly loved music; leaning on the pipa he composed two songs called Earth's Depth and Heaven's Height, expressing the meaning of husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Before reigning, Gaozu loved music and composed Earth's Depth and Heaven's Height on pipa as a husband-wife allegory.

sentences.zh: 因即取之為房內曲。

translations.literal: These were immediately taken as inner-chamber pieces.
translations.idiomatic: These became inner-chamber pieces.

sentences.zh: 命婦人並登歌上壽並用之。

translations.literal: Women were ordered to use them for ascent hymns and longevity toasts alike.
translations.idiomatic: Women performed them for ascent hymns and longevity toasts.

sentences.zh: 職在宮內，女人教習之。

translations.literal: The duty lay within the palace; women were trained in them.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women were trained to perform them.

sentences.zh: 初，後周故事，懸鐘磬法，七正七倍，合為十四。

translations.literal: Initially, in Later Zhou precedent, the method of suspended bells and chimes had seven orthodox and seven doubled, totaling fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou suspended bells and chimes used seven orthodox and seven doubled—fourteen total.

sentences.zh: 蓋准變宮、變徵，凡為七聲，有正有倍，而為十四也。

translations.literal: This followed altered palace and altered bell-note tones: seven tones in all, each with orthodox and doubled forms, making fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Seven tones, each orthodox and doubled, made fourteen.

sentences.zh: 長孫紹遠引《國語》冷州鳩云：「武王伐殷，歲在鶉火。

translations.literal: Changsun Shaoyuan cited the Guo Yu's Leng Zhoujiu: "When King Wu attacked Yin, the year was in Quail Fire."
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Shaoyuan cited the Guo Yu: Wu's attack on Yin fell in Quail Fire.

sentences.zh: 」自鶉及駟，七位故也。

translations.literal: From Quail through the Four Stallions is seven stations—hence seven.
translations.idiomatic: Quail through Four Stallions spans seven stations.

sentences.zh: 既以七同其數，而以律和其聲，於是有七律。

translations.literal: Having matched number with seven and harmonized sound with pitch pipes, there were seven tones.
translations.idiomatic: Seven stations matched seven tones.

sentences.zh: 又引《尚書大傳》「謂之七始」，其注云：「謂黃鐘、林鐘、太簇、南呂、姑洗、應鐘、蕤賓也。

translations.literal: He also cited the Great Commentary on the Documents' "called the seven beginnings," glossed: "Yellow Bell, Forest Bell, Great Cluster, Southern Pitch, Maiden Wash, Responding Bell, and Flourishing Guest."
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Documents commentary's seven beginnings: Yellow Bell, Forest Bell, Great Cluster, Southern Pitch, Maiden Wash, Responding Bell, Flourishing Guest.

sentences.zh: 」歌聲不應此者，皆去之。

translations.literal: Singing tones not matching these were all removed.
translations.idiomatic: Nonmatching singing tones were removed.

sentences.zh: 然據一均言也。

translations.literal: Yet this speaks of a single mode.
translations.idiomatic: This concerns a single mode.

sentences.zh: 宮、商、角、徵、羽為正，變宮、變徵為和，加倍而有十四焉。

translations.literal: Palace, commercial, horn, bell-note, and feather are orthodox; altered palace and altered bell-note are harmonizing—doubled, there are fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Palace, commercial, horn, bell-note, and feather are orthodox; altered palace and altered bell-note harmonize—fourteen when doubled.

sentences.zh: 又梁武帝加以濁倍，三七二十一而同為架，雖取繁會，聲不合古。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang added turbid doubles—three times seven equals twenty-one on the same frame; though richly combined, the sound did not match antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wudi added turbid doubles—twenty-one frames, unorthodox in sound.

sentences.zh: 又後魏時，公孫崇設鐘磬正倍，參懸之。

translations.literal: In Later Wei, Gongsun Chong set orthodox and doubled bells and chimes in triple suspension.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei's Gongsun Chong used triple suspension of orthodox and doubled bells and chimes.

sentences.zh: 弘等並以為非，而據《周官·小胥職》「懸鐘磬，半之為堵，全之為肆」。

translations.literal: Hong and others all deemed these wrong, citing the Rites of Zhou Minor Musician: "Suspend bells and chimes—half is a wall, the whole is a display."
translations.idiomatic: Hong rejected these, citing the Minor Musician: half a wall, whole a display.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄曰：「鐘磬編懸之，二八十六而在一虡。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "Bells and chimes are strung in rows—two eights, sixteen, on one frame."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan: two eights, sixteen bells and chimes per frame.

sentences.zh: 鐘一堵，磬一堵，謂之肆。

translations.literal: One wall of bells and one wall of chimes is called a display.
translations.idiomatic: One bell wall and one chime wall make a display.

sentences.zh: 」又引《樂緯》「宮為君，商為臣，君臣皆尊，各置一副，故加十四而懸十六」。

translations.literal: He also cited the Music Weft: "Palace is ruler, commercial is minister—both are honored, each set placed separately; hence add fourteen and suspend sixteen."
translations.idiomatic: The Music Weft honors ruler and minister separately—sixteen suspended.

sentences.zh: 又據漢成帝時，犍為水濱得石磬十六枚，此皆懸八之義也。

translations.literal: Also, in Emperor Cheng of Han's time, sixteen stone chimes were obtained at Qianwei on the riverbank—all meaning suspension by eights.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chengdi's sixteen Qianwei stone chimes also mean suspension by eights.

sentences.zh: 懸鐘磬法，每虡准之，懸八用七，不取近周之法懸七也。

translations.literal: The method of suspended bells and chimes: each frame follows this; suspend eight using seven—do not adopt the recent Zhou method of suspending seven.
translations.idiomatic: Each frame suspends eight using seven—not Later Zhou's seven.

sentences.zh: 又參用《儀禮》及《尚書大傳》，為宮懸陳布之法。

translations.literal: Also combining the Ceremonial Rites and Great Commentary on the Documents, they established the array for palace suspension.
translations.idiomatic: They combined Ceremonial Rites and Documents commentary for palace suspension layout.

sentences.zh: 北方北向，應鐘起西，磬次之，黃鐘次之，鐘次之，大呂次之，皆東陳。

translations.literal: North faces north; from Responding Bell westward, chimes next, Yellow Bell next, bells next, Great Pitch next—all arrayed east.
translations.idiomatic: North faces north: Responding Bell west, then chimes, Yellow Bell, bells, Great Pitch—all eastward.

sentences.zh: 一建鼓在其東，東鼓。

translations.literal: One set drum east of them, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One set drum east, facing east.

sentences.zh: 東方西向，太簇起北，磬次之，夾鐘次之，鐘次之，姑洗次之，皆南陳。

translations.literal: East faces west; from Great Cluster northward, chimes next, Pinched Bell next, bells next, Maiden Wash next—all arrayed south.
translations.idiomatic: East faces west: Great Cluster north, then chimes, Pinched Bell, bells, Maiden Wash—all southward.

sentences.zh: 一建鼓在其南，東鼓。

translations.literal: One set drum south of them, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One set drum south, facing east.

sentences.zh: 南方北向，中呂起東，鐘次之，蕤賓次之，磬次之，林鐘次之，皆西陳。

translations.literal: South faces north; from Middle Pitch eastward, bells next, Flourishing Guest next, chimes next, Forest Bell next—all arrayed west.
translations.idiomatic: South faces north: Middle Pitch east, then bells, Flourishing Guest, chimes, Forest Bell—all westward.

sentences.zh: 一建鼓在其西，西鼓。

translations.literal: One set drum west of them, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: One set drum west, facing west.

sentences.zh: 西方東向，夷則起南，鐘次之，南呂次之，磬次之，無射次之，皆北陳。

translations.literal: West faces east; from Levelled Pitch southward, bells next, Southern Pitch next, chimes next, Unattached Shoot next—all arrayed north.
translations.idiomatic: West faces east: Levelled Pitch south, then bells, Southern Pitch, chimes, Unattached Shoot—all northward.

sentences.zh: 一建鼓在其北，西鼓。

translations.literal: One set drum north of them, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: One set drum north, facing west.

sentences.zh: 其大射，則撤北面而加鉦鼓。

translations.literal: For the great archery rite, the north side is removed and cymbal drums added.
translations.idiomatic: Great archery removes the north side and adds cymbal drums.

sentences.zh: 祭天用雷鼓、雷鞀，祭地用靈鼓、靈鞀，宗廟用路鼓、路鞀。

translations.literal: Heaven sacrifice uses thunder drums and thunder hand-drums; earth sacrifice uses spirit drums and spirit hand-drums; ancestral temple uses road drums and road hand-drums.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven uses thunder drums; earth spirit drums; temple road drums.

sentences.zh: 各兩設在懸內。

translations.literal: Each pair is set within the suspension.
translations.idiomatic: Each pair stands within the suspension.

sentences.zh: 又准《儀禮》，宮懸四面設鎛鐘十二虡，各依辰位。

translations.literal: Also following the Ceremonial Rites, the palace hall sets twelve bo bell frames on four sides, each according to its branch position.
translations.idiomatic: Palace halls set twelve bo-bell frames by branch position.

sentences.zh: 又甲、丙、庚、壬位，各設鐘一虡，乙、丁、辛、癸位，各陳磬一虡。

translations.literal: At jia, bing, geng, and ren positions each set one bell frame; at yi, ding, xin, and gui positions each array one chime frame.
translations.idiomatic: Jia, bing, geng, ren get bell frames; yi, ding, xin, gui get chime frames.

sentences.zh: 共為二十虡。

translations.literal: Twenty frames in all.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty frames total.

sentences.zh: 其宗廟殿庭郊丘社並同。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple halls, palace courts, suburban mounds, and altars are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Temple halls, courts, suburban mounds, and altars follow the same layout.

sentences.zh: 樹建鼓於四隅，以象二十四氣。

translations.literal: Set drums are planted at the four corners to represent the twenty-four qi.
translations.idiomatic: Set drums at four corners represent twenty-four qi.

sentences.zh: 依月為均，四箱同作，蓋取毛傳《詩》云「四懸皆同」之義。

translations.literal: Following monthly modes, four boxes made alike—taking Mao's Commentary on the Odes' "all four suspensions are alike."
translations.idiomatic: Four identical boxes by monthly mode follow "all four suspensions alike."

sentences.zh: 古者鎛鐘據《儀禮》擊為節檢，而無合曲之義。

translations.literal: In antiquity bo bells, per the Ceremonial Rites, were struck as beat-checks and had no meaning of combining into pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient bo bells were beat-checks only—not full pieces.

sentences.zh: 又大射有二鎛，皆亂擊焉，乃無成曲之理。

translations.literal: Great archery also had two bo bells, all struck randomly—hence no completed piece.
translations.idiomatic: Great archery's two bo bells were struck randomly—no completed piece.

sentences.zh: 依後周以十二鎛相生擊之，聲韻克諧。

translations.literal: Following Later Zhou, twelve bo bells were struck in generating sequence—the tones harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou struck twelve bo bells in generating sequence—harmonious.

sentences.zh: 每鎛鐘、建鼓各一人。

translations.literal: Each bo bell and set drum had one performer.
translations.idiomatic: One performer per bo bell and set drum.

sentences.zh: 每鐘、磬簨虡各一人，歌二人，執節一人，琴、瑟、箏、築各一人。

translations.literal: Each bell and chime frame had one performer; two singers; one beat-keeper; one each on zither, se, zheng, and zhu.
translations.idiomatic: One performer per bell/chime frame; two singers; one beat-keeper; one each on zither, se, zheng, zhu.

sentences.zh: 每鐘虡，竽、笙、簫、笛、塤、篪各一人。

translations.literal: Each bell frame: one each on yu, sheng, xiao, di, xun, and chi.
translations.idiomatic: Each bell frame: yu, sheng, xiao, di, xun, chi—one each.

sentences.zh: 懸內柷、敔各一人，柷在東，吾在西。

translations.literal: Within the suspension, one each on zhu and yu—zhu east, yu west.
translations.idiomatic: Within suspension: zhu east, yu west—one each.

sentences.zh: 二舞各八佾。

translations.literal: Two dances, each with eight rows.
translations.idiomatic: Two dances, eight rows each.

sentences.zh: 樂人皆平巾幘、絳褠衣。

translations.literal: Musicians all wore plain kerchiefs and crimson-trimmed robes.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians wore plain kerchiefs and crimson-trimmed robes.

sentences.zh: 樂器並采《周官》，參之梁代，擇用其尤善者。

translations.literal: Instruments all followed the Rites of Zhou, consulting Liang and choosing the best.
translations.idiomatic: Instruments followed the Rites of Zhou, consulting Liang for the best.

sentences.zh: 其簨虡皆金五博山，飾以崇牙，樹羽旒蘇。

translations.literal: Their frames all had gold five-peaked mountains, ornamented with lofty teeth and planted with feather tassels and tassels of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Frames had gold five-peaked mountains, lofty teeth, feather tassels.

sentences.zh: 其樂器應漆者，天地之神皆硃漆，宗廟及殿庭則五色漆畫。

translations.literal: Instruments requiring lacquer: spirits of Heaven and Earth in cinnabar lacquer; ancestral temple and palace court in five-color lacquer painting.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven-and-Earth instruments in cinnabar lacquer; temple and court in five colors.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋故事，箱別各有柷、敔，既同時戛之，今則不用。

translations.literal: Jin and Song precedent had separate zhu and yu for each box, struck simultaneously; now these are not used.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Song struck zhu and yu per box simultaneously; now omitted.

sentences.zh: 又《周官·大司樂》：「奏黃鐘，歌大呂，舞《雲門》，以祀天神。

translations.literal: Also the Rites of Zhou Grand Music Master: "Play Yellow Bell, sing Great Pitch, dance Cloud Gate, to sacrifice to the Heavenly Spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Music Master: Yellow Bell, Great Pitch, Cloud Gate—for the Heavenly Spirit.

sentences.zh: 奏太簇，歌應鐘，舞《咸池》，以祭地祇。

translations.literal: Play Great Cluster, sing Responding Bell, dance Xian Chi, to sacrifice to earthly spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Great Cluster, Responding Bell, Xian Chi—for earthly spirits.

sentences.zh: 奏姑洗，歌南呂，舞《大韶》，以祀四望。

translations.literal: Play Maiden Wash, sing Southern Pitch, dance Great Shao, to sacrifice to the Four Outlooks.
translations.idiomatic: Maiden Wash, Southern Pitch, Great Shao—for the Four Outlooks.

sentences.zh: 奏蕤賓，歌函鐘，舞《大夏》，以祭山川。

translations.literal: Play Flourishing Guest, sing Enclosing Bell, dance Great Summer, to sacrifice to mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Flourishing Guest, Enclosing Bell, Great Summer—for mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 奏夷則，歌小呂，舞《大護》，以享先妣。

translations.literal: Play Levelled Pitch, sing Lesser Pitch, dance Great Shield, to enjoy the prior consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Levelled Pitch, Lesser Pitch, Great Shield—for prior consorts.

sentences.zh: 奏無射，歌夾鐘，舞《大武》，以享先祖。

translations.literal: Play Unattached Shoot, sing Pinched Bell, dance Great Martial, to enjoy the prior ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Unattached Shoot, Pinched Bell, Great Martial—for prior ancestors.

sentences.zh: 」此乃周制，立二王三恪，通己為六代之樂。

translations.literal: This is Zhou regulation, establishing two kings and three enfeoffed lines, six generations of music including one's own.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou established two kings and three enfeoffed lines—six generations of music.

sentences.zh: 至四時祭祀，則分而用之。

translations.literal: For the four seasonal sacrifices, these were divided and used.
translations.idiomatic: Four seasonal sacrifices divided their use.

sentences.zh: 以六樂配十二調，一代之樂，則用二調矣。

translations.literal: Matching six ritual musics with twelve modes, one generation's music used two modes.
translations.idiomatic: Six ritual musics matched twelve modes—two modes per generation.

sentences.zh: 隋去六代之樂，又無四望、先妣之祭，今既與古祭法有別，乃以神祗位次分樂配焉。

translations.literal: Sui removed the six dynasties' music and also had no sacrifices to the Four Outlooks or prior consorts; now differing from ancient sacrifice law, music was assigned by rank of spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Sui dropped six-dynasty music and Four Outlooks/consort rites—music now matched spirit rank.

sentences.zh: 奏黃鐘，歌大呂，以祀圓丘。

translations.literal: Play Yellow Bell, sing Great Pitch, to sacrifice at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell, Great Pitch—for the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘所以宣六氣也，耀魄天神，最為尊極，故奏黃鐘以祀之。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell expresses the six qi; the Bright Soul Heavenly Spirit is most exalted—hence Yellow Bell is played.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell expresses six qi; the Bright Soul Spirit is supreme.

sentences.zh: 奏太簇，歌應鐘，以祭方澤。

translations.literal: Play Great Cluster, sing Responding Bell, to sacrifice at the Square Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Great Cluster, Responding Bell—for the Square Pond.

sentences.zh: 太簇所以贊陽出滯，昆侖厚載之重，故奏太簇以祀之。

translations.literal: Great Cluster assists yang emerging from stagnation; Kunlun's heavy earth-burden is weighty—hence Great Cluster.
translations.idiomatic: Great Cluster assists yang; Kunlun's earth-burden is weighty.

sentences.zh: 奏姑洗，歌南呂，以祀五郊、神州。

translations.literal: Play Maiden Wash, sing Southern Pitch, to sacrifice at the Five Suburbs and Spirit Land.
translations.idiomatic: Maiden Wash, Southern Pitch—for Five Suburbs and Spirit Land.

sentences.zh: 姑洗所以滌潔百物，五郊神州，天地之次，故奏姑洗以祀之。

translations.literal: Maiden Wash cleanses the hundred things; Five Suburbs and Spirit Land are next to Heaven and Earth—hence Maiden Wash.
translations.idiomatic: Maiden Wash cleanses all things; suburbs rank below Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 奏蕤賓，歌函鐘，以祭宗廟。

translations.literal: Play Flourishing Guest, sing Enclosing Bell, to sacrifice at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Flourishing Guest, Enclosing Bell—for the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓所以安靜神人，祖宗有國之本，故奏蕤賓以祀之。

translations.literal: Flourishing Guest quiets spirits and people; ancestors are the root of the state—hence Flourishing Guest.
translations.idiomatic: Flourishing Guest quiets spirits and people; ancestors root the state.

sentences.zh: 奏夷則，歌小呂，以祭社稷、先農。

translations.literal: Play Levelled Pitch, sing Lesser Pitch, to sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain and Prior Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Levelled Pitch, Lesser Pitch—for soil-grain and Prior Agriculture altars.

sentences.zh: 夷則所以詠歌九穀，貴在秋成，故奏夷則以祀之。

translations.literal: Levelled Pitch sings of the nine grains; autumn harvest is prized—hence Levelled Pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Levelled Pitch celebrates the nine grains; autumn harvest is prized.

sentences.zh: 奏無射，歌夾鐘，以祭巡狩方嶽。

translations.literal: Play Unattached Shoot, sing Pinched Bell, to sacrifice at imperial tours and directional mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Unattached Shoot, Pinched Bell—for imperial tours and directional mountains.

sentences.zh: 無射所以示人軌物，觀風望秩，故奏無射以祀之。

translations.literal: Unattached Shoot displays human norms and things; observing customs and ranking honors—hence Unattached Shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Unattached Shoot displays norms; observing customs on tour.

sentences.zh: 同用文武二舞。

translations.literal: Both use the cultured and martial two dances.
translations.idiomatic: Both use cultured and martial dances.

sentences.zh: 其圓丘降神六變，方澤降神八變，宗廟禘祫降神九變，皆用《昭夏》。

translations.literal: For Round Mound spirit-descent six changes, Square Pond eight changes, and temple diqi nine changes—all use Bright Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Round Mound six changes, Square Pond eight, temple diqi nine—all use Bright Summer.

sentences.zh: 其餘祭享皆一變。

translations.literal: Other sacrificial feasts use one change each.
translations.idiomatic: Other sacrifices use one change each.

sentences.zh: 又《周禮》，王出，奏《王夏》，屍出，奏《肆夏》。

translations.literal: Also the Rites of Zhou: when the king goes out, play King Summer; when the corpse goes out, play Display Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Rites of Zhou: King Summer when the king goes out; Display Summer when the corpse departs.

sentences.zh: 叔孫通法，迎神奏《嘉至》。

translations.literal: Shusun Tong's method played Excellent Arrival to welcome the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Tong played Excellent Arrival to welcome spirits.

sentences.zh: 今亦隨事立名。

translations.literal: Now names are likewise established according to the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Names are now set by occasion.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入出，皆奏《皇夏》。

translations.literal: When the emperor enters or exits, Bright Summer is played.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's entry and exit use Bright Summer.

sentences.zh: 群官入出，皆奏《肆夏》。

translations.literal: When officials enter or exit, Display Summer is played.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' entry and exit use Display Summer.

sentences.zh: 食舉上壽，奏《需夏》。

translations.literal: For dish-raising and longevity toasts, Need Summer is played.
translations.idiomatic: Dish-raising and longevity toasts use Need Summer.

sentences.zh: 迎、送神，奏《昭夏》。

translations.literal: Welcoming and sending off spirits, Bright Summer is played.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming and sending spirits use Bright Summer.

sentences.zh: 薦獻郊廟，奏《誠夏》。

translations.literal: Offering at suburban altars and temples, Sincere Summer is played.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and temple offerings use Sincere Summer.

sentences.zh: 宴饗殿上，奏登歌。

translations.literal: At palace banquets, ascent hymns are played.
translations.idiomatic: Palace banquets use ascent hymns.

sentences.zh: 並文舞武舞，合為八曲。

translations.literal: Cultured and martial dances together make eight pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Cultured and martial dances total eight pieces.

sentences.zh: 古有宮、商、角、徵、羽五引，梁以三朝元會奏之。

translations.literal: Antiquity had five introductory pieces in palace, commercial, horn, bell-note, and feather; Liang played them at the three morning assemblies and New Year audience.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity had five introductory palace/commercial/horn/bell-note/feather pieces; Liang played them at New Year audiences.

sentences.zh: 今改為五音，其聲悉依宮商，不使差越。

translations.literal: Now these are changed to five tones; their sounds all follow palace and commercial without deviation.
translations.idiomatic: They become five tones following palace and commercial without deviation.

sentences.zh: 唯迎氣於五郊，降神奏之，《月令》所謂「孟春其音角」是也。

translations.literal: Only for qi-welcoming at the five suburbs is spirit-descent played—this is what the Monthly Ordinance means by "in early spring its tone is horn."
translations.idiomatic: Only five-suburb qi-welcoming plays spirit-descent—the Monthly Ordinance's "early spring horn tone."

sentences.zh: 通前為十三曲。

translations.literal: With the previous pieces, thirteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen pieces in all with the foregoing.

sentences.zh: 並內宮所奏《天高》、《地厚》二曲，于房中奏之，合十五曲。

translations.literal: Including the inner chamber's Heaven's Height and Earth's Depth, played in the inner chambers—fifteen pieces total.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-chamber Heaven's Height and Earth's Depth bring the total to fifteen.

sentences.zh: 其登歌法，准《禮·效特牲》「歌者在上，匏竹在下。

translations.literal: The ascent hymn method follows the Rites: "Singers above, gourd and bamboo below."
translations.idiomatic: Ascent hymns follow the Rites: singers above, gourd and bamboo below.

sentences.zh: 」《大戴》云：「清廟之歌，懸一磬而尚拊搏。

translations.literal: The Great Dai says: "In the Clear Temple hymn, one chime is suspended yet clapping is honored."
translations.idiomatic: Great Dai: Clear Temple hymns suspend one chime yet honor clapping.

sentences.zh: 」又在漢代，獨登歌者，不以絲竹亂人聲。

translations.literal: Also in Han times, ascent hymns alone were sung without strings and bamboo confusing human voices.
translations.idiomatic: Han ascent hymns used human voice alone without strings and bamboo.

sentences.zh: 近代以來，有登歌五人，別升於上，絲竹一部，進處階前。

translations.literal: In recent times, five ascent singers separately ascend while one section of strings and bamboo advances before the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Recently five ascent singers ascend separately while strings and bamboo wait on the steps.

sentences.zh: 此蓋《尚書》「戛擊鳴球，搏拊琴瑟以詠，祖考來格」之義也。

translations.literal: This follows the Documents: "Strike and tap sounding spheres, clap zither and se to sing—ancestors come near."
translations.idiomatic: This follows the Documents: strike spheres, clap zither and se—ancestors draw near.

sentences.zh: 梁武《樂論》以為登歌者頌祖宗功業，檢《禮記》乃非元日所奏。

translations.literal: Liang Wu's Music Treatise held ascent hymns praise ancestral achievement; checking the Book of Rites shows they are not for New Year's day.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu held ascent hymns praise ancestors; the Book of Rites excludes New Year's day.

sentences.zh: 若三朝大慶，百辟俱陳，升工籍殿，以詠祖考，君臣相對，便須涕洟。

translations.literal: If at the great New Year audience the hundred lords are all present and singers ascend the hall to chant ancestors, ruler and ministers face each other and tears must flow.
translations.idiomatic: At New Year, ruler and ministers facing ascent hymns to ancestors would weep.

sentences.zh: 以此說非通，還以嘉慶用之。

translations.literal: This reasoning is unsound; Bright Celebration is used instead.
translations.idiomatic: That view fails; Bright Celebration is used instead.

sentences.zh: 後周登歌，備鐘、磬、琴、瑟，階上設笙、管。

translations.literal: Later Zhou ascent hymns included bells, chimes, zither, and se; sheng and pipes were set on the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou ascent hymns added bells, chimes, zither, se; sheng and pipes on the steps.

sentences.zh: 今遂因之。

translations.literal: This precedent is now followed.
translations.idiomatic: That precedent is now followed.

sentences.zh: 合於《儀禮》荷瑟升歌，及笙入，立於階下，間歌合樂，是燕飲之事矣。

translations.literal: Matching the Ceremonial Rites' carrying se to ascend and sing, and when sheng enters standing below the steps, inter-song combined music—this is banquet matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Rites: carrying se to ascend, sheng below—banquet music.

sentences.zh: 登歌法，十有四人，鐘東磬西，工各一人，琴、瑟、箏、築各一人，並歌者三人，執節七人，並坐階上。

translations.literal: Ascent hymn method: fourteen persons—bells east, chimes west, one worker each; zither, se, zheng, zhu one each; three singers; seven beat-keepers—all seated on the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen ascent performers: bells east, chimes west; instruments and singers seated on steps.

sentences.zh: 笙、竽、簫、笛、塤、篪各一人，並立階下。

translations.literal: Sheng, yu, xiao, di, xun, chi—one each, standing below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, yu, xiao, di, xun, chi stand below the steps.

sentences.zh: 悉進賢冠，絳公服。

translations.literal: All wear advance-the-worthy caps and crimson court robes.
translations.idiomatic: All wear advance-the-worthy caps and crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 斟酌古今，參而用之。

translations.literal: Weighing ancient and modern, combine and use them.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern are weighed and combined.

sentences.zh: 祀神宴會通行之。

translations.literal: Used generally for spirit sacrifice and banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Used for spirit sacrifice and banquets alike.

sentences.zh: 若有大祀臨軒，陳於階壇之上。

translations.literal: For great sacrifices when the emperor faces the hall, they are arrayed on the step altar.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifices array them on the step altar.

sentences.zh: 若冊拜王公，設宮懸，不用登歌。

translations.literal: For investiture of princes and dukes, palace suspension is set but ascent hymns are not used.
translations.idiomatic: Princely investiture uses palace suspension without ascent hymns.

sentences.zh: 釋奠則唯用登歌，而不設懸。

translations.literal: Libation sacrifices use ascent hymns alone without suspension.
translations.idiomatic: Libation sacrifices use ascent hymns without suspension.

sentences.zh: 古者人君食，皆用當月之調，以取時律之聲。

translations.literal: In antiquity when the ruler ate, he used that month's mode to take the seasonal pitch-pipe's tone.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers ate to that month's pitch mode.

sentences.zh: 使不失五常之性，調暢四體，令得時氣之和。

translations.literal: Thus the five constants' nature was not lost and the four limbs harmonized, obtaining seasonal qi's harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the five constants and four limbs harmonized with seasonal qi.

sentences.zh: 故鮑鄴上言，天子食飲，必順四時，有食舉樂，所以順天地，養神明，可作十二月均，感天和氣。

translations.literal: Hence Bao Ye's memorial: the Son of Heaven's food and drink must follow the four seasons; dish-raising music accords Heaven and Earth, nourishes spirits—twelve monthly modes may be made to move Heaven's harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Ye urged twelve monthly modes so royal meals would move Heaven's qi.

sentences.zh: 此則殿庭月調之義也。

translations.literal: This is the meaning of monthly modes in the palace court.
translations.idiomatic: This is palace monthly-mode doctrine.

sentences.zh: 祭祀既已分樂，臨軒朝會，並用當月之律。

translations.literal: Since sacrifices already divide music, court audiences likewise use that month's pitch law.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices divide music; court audiences use the month's pitch law.

sentences.zh: 正月懸太簇之均，乃至十二月懸大呂之均，欲感君人情性，允協陰陽之序也。

translations.literal: First month suspends Great Cluster mode through twelfth month Great Pitch mode—intending to move the ruler's disposition and harmonize yin and yang's order.
translations.idiomatic: Month 1 Great Cluster through month 12 Great Pitch moves the ruler's heart and yin-yang order.

sentences.zh: 又文舞六十四人，並黑介幘，冠進賢冠，絳紗連裳，內單，皁褾、領、襈、裾、革帶，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Also the cultured dance: sixty-four persons, all black kerchiefs, advance-the-worthy caps, crimson gauze linked robes, inner single garment, black border, collar, flap, hem, leather belt, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Cultured dance: sixty-four in black kerchiefs, advance-the-worthy caps, crimson linked robes.

sentences.zh: 十六人執鸑。

translations.literal: Sixteen hold yu feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen hold yu feathers.

sentences.zh: 十六人執Ｏ。

translations.literal: Sixteen hold [dance implements].
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen hold [implements].

sentences.zh: 十六人執旄。

translations.literal: Sixteen hold yak-tail banners.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen hold yak-tail banners.

sentences.zh: 十六人執羽，左手皆執籥。

translations.literal: Sixteen hold plumes; in the left hand all hold yue flutes.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen hold plumes; left hand holds yue flutes.

sentences.zh: 二人執纛，引前，在舞人數外，衣冠同舞人。

translations.literal: Two hold streamers, leading in front, outside the dancers—dress same as dancers.
translations.idiomatic: Two streamer-bearers lead outside the dancers.

sentences.zh: 武舞六十四人，並服武弁，硃褠衣，革帶，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Martial dance: sixty-four persons, all martial caps, cinnabar-trimmed robes, leather belts, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Martial dance: sixty-four in martial caps and cinnabar-trimmed robes.

sentences.zh: 左執硃幹，右執大戚，依硃幹玉戚之文。

translations.literal: Left hand holds cinnabar shield; right hand holds great axe—following the cinnabar shield and jade axe text.
translations.idiomatic: Left cinnabar shield, right great axe—jade-axe style.

sentences.zh: 二人執旌，居前，二人執鞀，二人執鐸。

translations.literal: Two hold banners in front; two hold hand-drums; two hold bells.
translations.idiomatic: Two banners, two hand-drums, two bells in front.

sentences.zh: 金錞二，四人輿，二人作。

translations.literal: Two metal chun, four carrying them, two playing.
translations.idiomatic: Two metal chun, four carriers, two players.

sentences.zh: 二人執鐃次之。

translations.literal: Two hold cymbals next.
translations.idiomatic: Two cymbals next.

sentences.zh: 二人執相，在左，二人執雅，在右，各工一人作。

translations.literal: Two hold xiang left; two hold ya right—one worker each.
translations.idiomatic: Two xiang left, two ya right—one player each.

sentences.zh: 自旌以下來引，並在舞人數外，衣冠同舞人。

translations.literal: From banners downward all lead outside the dancers—dress same as dancers.
translations.idiomatic: Banner-bearers and leaders stand outside the dancers.

sentences.zh: 《周官》所謂「以金錞和鼓，金鐲節鼓，金鐃止鼓，金鐸通鼓」也。

translations.literal: This is what the Rites of Zhou means by "use metal chun to harmonize drums, metal duo to beat drums, metal nao to stop drums, metal duo to signal drums."
translations.idiomatic: Rites of Zhou: metal chun harmonizes drums, duo beats, nao stops, duo signals.

sentences.zh: 又依《樂記》象德擬功，初來就位，總幹而山立，思君道之難也。

translations.literal: Also following the Record of Music's modeling virtue and achievement: first arriving and taking position, gathering shields and standing like a mountain—thinking on the ruler's way's difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Record of Music: gathering shields mountain-high recalls the ruler's difficult path.

sentences.zh: 發揚蹈厲，威而不殘也。

translations.literal: Expanding and treading vigorously—awe without cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Expanding and treading vigorously—awe without cruelty.

sentences.zh: 舞亂皆坐，四海咸安也。

translations.literal: When the dance disorder all sit—within the four seas all is peace.
translations.idiomatic: When disorder ends all sit—all within the seas at peace.

sentences.zh: 武，始而受命，再成而定山東，三成而平蜀道，四成而北狄是通，五成而江南是拓，六成復綴，以闡太平。

translations.literal: Martial: first movement receiving the mandate; second securing Shandong; third pacifying the Shu road; fourth opening the northern barbarians; fifth extending into Jiangnan; sixth returning to the sequence, proclaiming great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Martial: six movements—from mandate through Shandong, Shu, north, Jiangnan, to great peace.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「不須象功德，直象事可也。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "No need to model achievements—model events directly."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "Model events, not achievements."

sentences.zh: 」然竟用之。

translations.literal: Yet they were used after all.
translations.idiomatic: They were used anyway.

sentences.zh: 近代舞出入皆作樂，謂之階步，咸用《肆夏》。

translations.literal: In recent times dance entry and exit all had music, called step music—all using Display Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Recent dance entry and exit used step music—Display Summer.

sentences.zh: 今亦依定，即《周官》所謂樂出入奏鐘鼓也。

translations.literal: Now this is fixed—it is what the Rites of Zhou means by playing bells and drums at music entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: Now fixed—the Rites of Zhou's bells and drums at entry and exit.

sentences.zh: 又魏、晉故事，有《矛俞》、《弩俞》及硃儒導引。

translations.literal: Also Wei and Jin precedent had Spear Dance, Crossbow Dance, and cinnabar Confucians as guides.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin also had Spear Dance, Crossbow Dance, and cinnabar Confucian guides.

sentences.zh: 今據《尚書》直雲干羽，《禮》文稱羽籥干戚。

translations.literal: Now according to the Documents it simply says shield and plume; ritual texts say plume-flute, shield, and axe.
translations.idiomatic: Documents say shield and plume; ritual texts plume-flute, shield, axe.

sentences.zh: 今文舞執羽籥，武舞執干戚，其《矛俞》、《弩俞》等，蓋漢高祖自漢中歸，巴、俞之兵，執仗而舞也。

translations.literal: Now cultured dance holds plume-flute; martial dance holds shield and axe—the Spear and Crossbow dances likely came when Han Gaozu returned from Hanzhong with Ba and Yu troops dancing with weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Cultured dance uses plume-flute; martial shield and axe—Spear and Crossbow likely came from Hanzhong Ba-Yu troops.

sentences.zh: 既非正典，悉罷不用。

translations.literal: Since these are not orthodox canon, all are abolished and not used.
translations.idiomatic: Non-orthodox pieces are abolished.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，樂定。

translations.literal: Third month of the fourteenth year—the music was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Month 3, year 14—the music was fixed.

sentences.zh: 秘書監、奇章縣公牛弘，秘書丞、北絳郡公姚察，通直散騎常侍、虞部侍郎許善心，兼內史舍人虞世基，儀同三司、東宮學士饒陽伯劉臻等奏曰：「臣聞蕢桴土鼓，由來斯尚，雷出地奮，著自《易經》。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director and Qizhang County Duke Niu Hong, Secretariat Aide and Beijiang Commandery Duke Yao Cha, Palace Attendant and Yu Department Vice Minister Xu Shanxin, Concurrent Palace Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shiji, Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes and Eastern Palace Scholar Raoyang Marquis Liu Zhen and others memorialized: "Your subject has heard that earthen drums and earthen drums have been honored from old; thunder emerging from earth and leaping forth is recorded in the Changes."
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong, Yao Cha, Xu Shanxin, Yu Shiji, Liu Zhen and others memorialized on music's ancient honor.

sentences.zh: 邃古帝王，經邦馭物，揖讓而臨天下者，祀樂之謂也。

translations.literal: Remote ancient emperors, governing the state and mastering things, yielding the throne and facing all under Heaven—this is what sacrificial music means.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient emperors governed through sacrificial music.

sentences.zh: 秦焚經典，樂書亡缺，爰至漢興，始加鳩采，祖述增廣，緝成朝憲。

translations.literal: Qin burned the classics and music books were lost; only when Han rose did collection begin, inheriting and expanding into court law.
translations.idiomatic: Qin burned classics; Han began collecting music into court law.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉相承，更加論討，沿革之宜，備於故實。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin handed down and added further discussion—the appropriateness of succession and change is fully recorded in old fact.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin added discussion recorded in precedent.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之後，九服崩離，燕、石、苻、姚，遁據華土。

translations.literal: After Yongjia the nine domains collapsed; Yan, Shi, Fu, and Yao seized and held the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongjia the realm collapsed; barbarian states held the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 此其戎乎，何必伊川之上，吾其左衽，無復微管之功。

translations.literal: These were barbarians—why must it be above the Yi River? Our left lapels—no more Guan Zhong's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians everywhere—not only beyond the Yi; left lapels, no Guan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 前言往式，於斯而盡。

translations.literal: The former patterns end here.
translations.idiomatic: Former patterns ended there.

sentences.zh: 金陵建社，朝士南奔，帝則皇規，粲然更備，與內原隔絕，三百年於茲矣。

translations.literal: Jinling established its altar; court scholars fled south—the imperial regulations brilliantly renewed, yet cut off from the inner heartland for three hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling rose; scholars fled south—three centuries cut off from the heartland.

sentences.zh: 伏惟明聖膺期，會昌在運。

translations.literal: Your subject reverently considers that enlightened sagacity received the era; flourishing brilliance is in fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Enlightened sagacity received the era; fortune flourishes.

sentences.zh: 今南征所獲梁、陳樂人，及晉、宋旗章，宛然俱至。

translations.literal: Now musicians of Liang and Chen captured in the southern campaign, and Jin and Song banners and standards, have all duly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Liang-Chen musicians and Jin-Song regalia have all arrived.

sentences.zh: 曩代所不服者，今悉服之，前朝所未得者，今悉得之。

translations.literal: What former ages did not submit to now all submit; what former dynasties did not obtain now all obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Former non-submitters submit; former lacks are filled.

sentences.zh: 化洽功成，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Transformation harmonized and achievement complete—here it is.
translations.idiomatic: Transformation harmonized, achievement complete.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏奉明詔，詳定雅樂，博訪知音，旁求儒彥，研校是非，定其去就，取為一代正樂，具在本司。

translations.literal: Your subjects reverently received the clear edict, thoroughly fixing court ritual music, broadly seeking those who know tone, seeking Confucian talents on all sides, examining right and wrong and fixing what to keep or discard, taking this as one generation's orthodox music—all detailed in this office.
translations.idiomatic: We fixed court music as one generation's orthodox repertoire.

sentences.zh: 」於是並撰歌辭三十首，詔並令施用，見行者皆停之。

translations.literal: Thereupon thirty song texts were composed together; an edict ordered all applied, and whatever was in practice was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty song texts were composed; edict ordered their use and stopped old practice.

sentences.zh: 其人間音樂，流僻日久，棄其舊體者，並加禁約，務存其本。

translations.literal: Popular music long flowing in vulgar ways, abandoning its old form—all were restricted to preserve the root.
translations.idiomatic: Popular music was restricted to preserve its root.

sentences.zh: 先是高祖遣內史侍郎李元操、直內史省盧思道等，列清廟歌辭十二曲。

translations.literal: Earlier Gaozu dispatched Palace Secretariat Gentleman Li Yuancao, Direct Palace Secretariat Gentleman Lu Simao, and others to compose twelve Clear Temple song texts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gaozu had Li Yuancao and Lu Simao compose twelve Clear Temple lyrics.

sentences.zh: 令齊樂人曹妙達于太樂教習，以代周歌。

translations.literal: Qi musicians Cao Miaoda were ordered to teach them at the Grand Music Office to replace Zhou songs.
translations.idiomatic: Qi musician Cao Miaoda taught them at Grand Music to replace Zhou songs.

sentences.zh: 其初迎神七言，象《元基曲》，獻奠登歌六言，象《傾杯曲》，送神禮畢五言，象《行天曲》。

translations.literal: Initially spirit-welcoming was seven-character lines, modeled on the Yuan Ji piece; offering and ascent hymn six-character, modeled on the Tilting Cup piece; spirit-send when rites complete five-character, modeled on the Traveling Heaven piece.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit-welcoming modeled Yuan Ji; offering ascent Tilting Cup; spirit-send Traveling Heaven.

sentences.zh: 至是弘等但改其聲，合于鐘律，而辭經敕定，不敢易之。

translations.literal: Now Hong and others only changed the sounds to match bell and pitch law; the texts were fixed by edict and dared not be altered.
translations.idiomatic: Hong changed sounds to match pitch law but kept edict-fixed texts.

sentences.zh: 至仁壽元年，煬帝初為皇太子，從饗于太廟，聞而非之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou, when Yangdi first became Crown Prince, attending sacrifice at the Grand Temple, he heard them and disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou 1, Crown Prince Yangdi disapproved at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 乃上言曰：「清廟歌辭，文多浮麗，不足以述宣功德，請更議定。

translations.literal: He submitted: "Clear Temple song texts are overly ornate and insufficient to proclaim merit—please reconsider and fix them."
