translations.idiomatic: He petitioned: Clear Temple lyrics are too ornate to proclaim merit—revise them.

sentences.zh: 」於是制詔吏部尚書、奇章公弘，開府儀同三司、領太子洗馬柳顧言，秘書丞、攝太常少卿許善心，內史舍人虞世基，禮部侍郎蔡徵等，更詳故實，創制雅樂歌辭。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Ministry of Personnel Director and Qizhang Duke Hong, Commissioner Opening the Office Equal to the Three Dukes and Concurrent Crown Prince Preceptor Liu Yiyan, Secretariat Aide and Acting Vice Director of Ceremonies Xu Shanxin, Palace Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shiji, Ministry of Rites Vice Director Cai Zheng and others to examine old fact in detail and create new court ritual song texts.
translations.idiomatic: Edict ordered Hong, Liu Yiyan, Xu Shanxin, Yu Shiji, Cai Zheng to create new court ritual lyrics.

sentences.zh: 其祠圓丘，皇帝入，至版位定，奏《昭夏》之樂，以降天神。

translations.literal: For Round Mound sacrifice: when the emperor enters, reaches the spirit tablet position and stands fixed, Bright Summer is played to descend the heavenly spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Round Mound: emperor enters, Bright Summer descends the heavenly spirit.

sentences.zh: 升壇，奏《皇夏》之樂。

translations.literal: Ascending the altar, Bright Summer is played.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending the altar: Bright Summer.

sentences.zh: 受玉帛，登歌，奏《昭夏》之樂。

translations.literal: Receiving jade and silk, ascent hymn, Bright Summer is played.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving jade and silk: ascent hymn Bright Summer.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降南陛，詣罍洗，洗爵訖，升壇，並奏《皇夏》。

translations.literal: The emperor descends the south steps, goes to the libation wash, finishes washing the cup, ascends the altar—all play Bright Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Descent, libation wash, re-ascent—all Bright Summer.

sentences.zh: 初升壇，俎入，奏《昭夏》之樂。

translations.literal: On first ascending the altar, when the meat stands enter, Bright Summer is played.
translations.idiomatic: First altar ascent with meat stands: Bright Summer.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初獻，奏《諴夏》之樂。

translations.literal: The emperor's first offering: Sincere Summer.
translations.idiomatic: First offering: Sincere Summer.

sentences.zh: 皇帝既獻，作文舞之舞。

translations.literal: After the emperor's offering, the cultured dance is performed.
translations.idiomatic: After offering: cultured dance.

sentences.zh: 皇帝飲福酒，作《需夏》之樂。

translations.literal: The emperor drinks the blessing wine: Need Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing wine: Need Summer.

sentences.zh: 皇帝反爵于坫，還本位，奏《皇夏》之樂。

translations.literal: The emperor returns the cup to the stand and returns to position: Bright Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Cup returned to stand: Bright Summer.

sentences.zh: 武舞出，作《肆夏》之樂。

translations.literal: The martial dance exits: Display Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Martial dance exit: Display Summer.

sentences.zh: 送神作《昭夏》之樂。

translations.literal: Sending off the spirits: Bright Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit send-off: Bright Summer.

sentences.zh: 就燎位，還大次，並奏《皇夏》。

translations.literal: Taking the kindling position and returning to the great tent: all play Bright Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Kindling and return to tent: Bright Summer.

sentences.zh: 圜丘：

translations.literal: Round Mound:
translations.idiomatic: Round Mound:

sentences.zh: 降神，奏《昭夏》辭：

translations.literal: Spirit descent, Bright Summer lyrics:
translations.idiomatic: Spirit descent—Bright Summer lyrics:

sentences.zh: 肅祭典，協良辰。

translations.literal: Solemn is the sacrificial canon; the auspicious day is aligned.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn rites on an aligned auspicious day.

sentences.zh: 具嘉薦，俟皇臻。

translations.literal: Fine offerings are prepared; awaiting the emperor's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Fine offerings await the emperor.

sentences.zh: 禮方成，樂已變。

translations.literal: The rite is just complete; the music has already changed.
translations.idiomatic: Rite complete, music changed.

sentences.zh: 感靈心，回天眷。

translations.literal: Moving the spirit heart, turning Heaven's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's favor moves the spirit heart.

sentences.zh: 辟華闕，下乾宮。

translations.literal: Opening the flowery gate, descending to the Qian palace.
translations.idiomatic: Opening the gate, descending to Qian.

sentences.zh: 乘精氣，禦祥風。

translations.literal: Riding refined qi, commanding auspicious wind.
translations.idiomatic: Riding refined qi, commanding auspicious wind.

sentences.zh: 望爟火，通田燭。

translations.literal: Gazing at the brazier fire, linking field candles.
translations.idiomatic: Brazier fire links field candles.

sentences.zh: 膺介圭，受瑄玉。

translations.literal: Receiving the jade tablet, accepting the round jade.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving tablet and round jade.

sentences.zh: 神之臨，慶陰陽。

translations.literal: The spirit descends—celebrating yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit descends—yin and yang rejoice.

sentences.zh: 煙衢洞，宸路深。

translations.literal: Smoke paths open; the imperial way runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: Smoke paths open; the imperial way deep.

sentences.zh: 善既福，德斯輔。

translations.literal: Goodness brings blessing; virtue assists.
translations.idiomatic: Goodness blesses; virtue assists.

sentences.zh: 流鴻祚，遍區宇。

translations.literal: Flowing great fortune fills the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Great fortune fills the realm.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升壇，奏《皇夏》辭：

translations.literal: The emperor ascends the altar, Bright Summer lyrics:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor ascends altar—Bright Summer:

sentences.zh: 於穆我君，昭明有融。

translations.literal: Grand and reverent is our lord, bright and merging in radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Grand our lord, bright in radiance.

sentences.zh: 道濟區域，功格玄穹。

translations.literal: The Way aids the realm; merit reaches the dark vault.
translations.idiomatic: The Way aids the realm; merit reaches heaven.

sentences.zh: 百神警衛，萬國承風，仁深德厚，信洽義豐。

translations.literal: The hundred spirits stand guard; ten thousand states receive the wind; benevolence deep, virtue thick, trust harmonized, righteousness abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits guard; states receive the wind—deep benevolence, thick virtue.

sentences.zh: 明發思政，勤憂在躬。

translations.literal: At dawn he reflects and governs; diligent care is in his person.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he governs; care is in his person.

sentences.zh: 鴻基惟永，福祚長隆。

translations.literal: The great foundation is eternal; fortune and eminence long flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Foundation eternal; fortune long flourishes.

sentences.zh: 登歌辭：

translations.literal: Ascent hymn lyrics:
translations.idiomatic: Ascent hymn:

sentences.zh: 德深禮大，道高饗穆。

translations.literal: Virtue deep, rites great; the Way high, feasting solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Deep virtue, great rites; high Way, solemn feast.

sentences.zh: 就陽斯恭，陟配惟肅。

translations.literal: Approaching yang with reverence; ascending to match with solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent toward yang; solemn in ascent.

sentences.zh: 血紘升氣，冕裘標服。

translations.literal: Blood threads rise as qi; robe and fur mark the garb.
translations.idiomatic: Blood threads rise; robe and fur mark the garb.

sentences.zh: 誠感清玄，信陳史祝。

translations.literal: Sincerity moves the clear dark; faith presents the historiographer's prayer.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity moves heaven; faith presents the prayer.

sentences.zh: 祗承靈貺，載膺多福。

translations.literal: Reverently receiving spirit blessing, bearing many fortunes.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently receiving blessing, bearing fortune.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初獻，奏《諴夏》辭：

translations.literal: The emperor's first offering, Sincere Summer lyrics:
translations.idiomatic: First offering—Sincere Summer:

sentences.zh: 肇禋崇祀，大報尊靈。

translations.literal: Beginning the border sacrifice, great report honoring the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Border sacrifice begins—great report to the spirit.

sentences.zh: 因高盡敬，掃地推誠。

translations.literal: Following the height with utmost reverence; sweeping earth, extending sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Utmost reverence on high; sweeping earth in sincerity.

translations.literal: eight in bell-note mode, Forest Bell;
translations.idiomatic: eight bell-note mode, Forest Bell;

sentences.zh: 二十五曲羽調，南呂也；

translations.literal: twenty-five in feather mode, Southern Pitch;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-five feather mode, Southern Pitch;

sentences.zh: 一十三曲變宮調，應鐘也。

translations.literal: thirteen in altered palace mode, Responding Bell.
translations.idiomatic: thirteen altered palace, Responding Bell.

sentences.zh: 其曲大抵以詩為本，參以古調，漸欲播之弦歌，被之金石。

translations.literal: The pieces mostly took poems as foundation, consulting ancient modes, gradually intending to spread them in string song and clothe them in metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Pieces took poems as base, consulting ancient modes for string and metal.

sentences.zh: 仍屬戎車，不遑刊正，禮樂之事，竟無成功焉。

translations.literal: Still belonging to war chariots, no leisure to publish and correct—rites and music ultimately achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: War left no leisure to publish—rites and music achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 自漢至梁、陳樂工，其大數不相逾越。

translations.literal: From Han through Liang and Chen, musicians' great numbers did not much exceed each other.
translations.idiomatic: Han through Liang-Chen musician numbers did not much differ.

sentences.zh: 及周並齊，隋並陳，各得其樂工，多為編戶。

translations.literal: When Zhou annexed Qi and Sui annexed Chen, each obtained their musicians—most were registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou took Qi musicians; Sui took Chen's—mostly registered households.

sentences.zh: 至六年，帝乃大括魏、齊、周、陳樂人子弟，悉配太常，並於關中為坊置之，其數益多前代。

translations.literal: By the sixth year, the Emperor greatly gathered Wei, Qi, Zhou, and Chen musician families and youths, all assigned to the Director of Ceremonies and placed in wards in Guanzhong—the number exceeded former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Year 6 gathered Wei-Qi-Zhou-Chen musicians into Guanzhong wards—exceeding former ages.

sentences.zh: 顧言等又奏，仙都宮內，四時祭享，還用太廟之樂，歌功論德，別制其辭。

translations.literal: Yiyan and others also memorialized: within the Immortal Capital Palace, four-season sacrifices still used Grand Temple music; singing achievement and discussing virtue separately made their texts.
translations.idiomatic: Immortal Capital sacrifices used Grand Temple music with separate merit lyrics.

sentences.zh: 七廟同院，樂依舊式。

translations.literal: Seven temples same courtyard; music followed old form.
translations.idiomatic: Seven temples one courtyard; old music form.

sentences.zh: 又造饗宴殿庭宮懸樂器，布陳簨虡，大抵同前，而於四隅各加二建鼓、三案。

translations.literal: Also made banquet hall palace suspension instruments, arraying frames— broadly same as before, but at four corners adding two set drums and three stands each.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet hall suspension like before but four corners gained set drums and stands.

sentences.zh: 又設十二鎛，鎛別鐘磬二架，各依辰位為調，合三十六架。

translations.literal: Also set twelve bo bells; each bo bell separate bell and chime two frames, each by branch position as mode—thirty-six frames total.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve bo bells, thirty-six frames by branch position.

sentences.zh: 至於音律節奏，皆依雅曲，意在演令繁會，自梁武帝之始也，開皇時，廢不用，至是又復焉。

translations.literal: As for pitch law and rhythm, all followed elegant pieces—intending elaborate command and rich assembly, from Liang Wudi's beginning; abandoned in Kaihuang, now restored.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch and rhythm followed elegant pieces—Liang style restored after Kaihuang abandonment.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，宮懸樂器，唯有一部，殿庭饗宴用之。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's time, palace suspension instruments had only one set, used for palace court banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had one palace suspension set for banquets.

sentences.zh: 平陳所獲，又有二部，宗廟郊丘分用之。

translations.literal: From pacifying Chen two more sets were obtained; ancestral temple and suburban mound used separately.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying Chen brought two more sets for temple and suburb.

sentences.zh: 至是並于樂府藏而不用。

translations.literal: Now all stored in the Music Office and not used.
translations.idiomatic: All stored unused in the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 更造三部：五郊二十架，工一百四十三人。

translations.literal: Three new sets made: Five Suburbs twenty frames, one hundred forty-three workers.
translations.idiomatic: Three new sets: Five Suburbs 20 frames, 143 workers.

sentences.zh: 廟庭二十架，工一百五十人。

translations.literal: Temple court twenty frames, one hundred fifty workers.
translations.idiomatic: Temple court 20 frames, 150 workers.

sentences.zh: 饗宴二十架，工一百七人。

translations.literal: Banquet twenty frames, one hundred seven workers.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet 20 frames, 107 workers.

sentences.zh: 舞郎各二等，並一百三十二人。

translations.literal: Dance youths two grades each, one hundred thirty-two persons total.
translations.idiomatic: Dance youths two grades, 132 persons.

sentences.zh: 顧言又增房內樂，益其鐘磬，奏議曰：「房內樂者，主為王后弦歌諷誦而事君子，故以房室為名。

translations.literal: Yiyan also increased inner-chamber music, adding its bells and chimes, memorializing: "Inner-chamber music mainly has the queen string-sing and recite to serve the lord—hence named for the inner chamber."
translations.idiomatic: Yiyan increased inner-chamber music: queen's string songs serving the lord.

sentences.zh: 燕禮饗飲酒禮，亦取而用也。

translations.literal: Banquet rites and drinking rites also take and use it.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet and drinking rites also use it.

sentences.zh: 故云：'用之鄉人焉，用之邦國焉。

translations.literal: Hence it says: "Use it among village people; use it among the state."
translations.idiomatic: "Use among village people; use among the state."

sentences.zh: '文王之風，由近及遠，鄉樂以感人，須存雅正。

translations.literal: King Wen's winds, from near to far—village music to move people must preserve elegant correctness.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen's winds from near to far—village music must stay elegant.

sentences.zh: 既不設鐘鼓，義無四懸，何以取正於婦道也。

translations.literal: Since bells and drums are not set, ritually there is no four-side suspension—how take correctness from women's Way?
translations.idiomatic: Without bells and drums, how can women's Way be corrected?

sentences.zh: 《磬師職》云：'燕樂之鐘磬。

translations.literal: The Chime Master office says: "Banquet music's bells and chimes."
translations.idiomatic: Chime Master: banquet music bells and chimes.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄曰：'燕樂，房內樂也，所謂陰聲，金石備矣。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "Banquet music is inner-chamber music—the so-called yin sound; metal and stone complete."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan: banquet music is inner-chamber yin sound with metal and stone.

sentences.zh: '以此而論，房內之樂，非獨弦歌，必有鐘磬也。

translations.literal: Judging from this, inner-chamber music is not strings alone—there must be bells and chimes.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-chamber music requires bells and chimes, not strings alone.

sentences.zh: 《內宰職》云：'正後服位，詔其禮樂之儀。

translations.literal: The Inner Steward office says: "Correct the queen's position; announce her rites and music protocol."
translations.idiomatic: Inner Steward: correct queen's position; announce rites and music.

sentences.zh: '鄭玄云：'薦撤之禮，當與樂相應。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan: "Offering and withdrawal rites should correspond with music."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan: offering and withdrawal should match music.

sentences.zh: '薦撤之言，雖施祭祀，其入出賓客，理亦宜同。

translations.literal: Offering and withdrawal words, though applied to sacrifice, entering and exiting guests—reason likewise should be same.
translations.idiomatic: Offering and withdrawal logic applies to guests as to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 請以歌鐘歌磬，各設二虡，土革絲竹並副之，並升歌下管，總名房內之樂。

translations.literal: Please set song bells and song chimes, two frames each; earth, leather, silk, bamboo all assisting; ascent song and lower pipes together—collectively named inner-chamber music.
translations.idiomatic: Song bells and chimes two frames each; ascent and lower pipes—inner-chamber music.

sentences.zh: 女奴肄習，朝燕用之。

translations.literal: Female servants trained; used at court banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Female servants trained for court banquets.

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「可。

translations.literal: Edict: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: Edict: Approved.

sentences.zh: 」於是內宮懸二十虡。

translations.literal: Thereupon inner palace suspension twenty frames.
translations.idiomatic: Inner palace suspension: twenty frames.

sentences.zh: 其鎛鐘十二，皆以大磬充。

translations.literal: Its twelve bo bells all filled with large chimes.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve bo bells filled with large chimes.

sentences.zh: 去建鼓，餘飾並與殿庭同。

translations.literal: Set drums removed; remaining ornament same as hall court.
translations.idiomatic: Set drums removed; ornament as hall court.

sentences.zh: 皇太子軒懸，去南面，設三鎛鐘于辰醜申，三建鼓亦如之。

translations.literal: Crown Prince elevated suspension, south removed; three bo bells at chen, chou, shen; three set drums likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince suspension: south removed; bo bells and set drums at chen, chou, shen.

sentences.zh: 編鐘三虡，編磬三虡，共三鎛鐘為九虡。

translations.literal: Strung bells three frames, strung chimes three frames—with three bo bells nine frames total.
translations.idiomatic: Three bell frames, three chime frames—nine with bo bells.

sentences.zh: 其登歌減者二人。

translations.literal: Ascent singers reduced by two.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent singers reduced by two.

sentences.zh: 簨虡金三博山。

translations.literal: Frames gold three-peaked mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Frames: gold three-peaked mountains.

sentences.zh: 樂器應漆者硃漆之。

translations.literal: Instruments requiring lacquer: cinnabar lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: Lacquered instruments: cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 其二舞用六佾。

translations.literal: Its two dances use six rows.
translations.idiomatic: Two dances: six rows each.

sentences.zh: 其雅樂鼓吹，多依開皇之故。

translations.literal: Its court ritual music and wind-and-drum mostly followed Kaihuang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual and wind-and-drum mostly followed Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 雅樂合二十器，今列之如左：

translations.literal: Court ritual music totals twenty instruments; now listed at left:
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual music: twenty instruments listed below:

sentences.zh: 金之屬二：一曰鎛鐘，每鐘懸一簨虡，各應律呂之音，即黃帝所命伶倫鑄十二鐘，和五音者也。

translations.literal: Metal category, two: first, bo bell—each bell one frame, each matching pitch-pipe tone; this is what the Yellow Emperor commanded Ling Lun to cast twelve bells harmonizing five tones.
translations.idiomatic: Metal: bo bell—Ling Lun's twelve bells harmonizing five tones.

sentences.zh: 二曰編鐘，小鐘也，各應律呂，大小以次，編而懸之。

translations.literal: Second, strung bells—small bells, each matching pitch pipes, large and small in sequence, strung and suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Strung bells—small bells strung by pitch size.

sentences.zh: 上下皆八，合十六鐘，懸於一簨虡。

translations.literal: Upper and lower each eight, sixteen bells total, suspended on one frame.
translations.idiomatic: Upper and lower eight each—sixteen on one frame.

sentences.zh: 石之屬一：曰磬，用玉若石為之，懸如編鐘之法。

translations.literal: Stone category, one: called chime—made of jade or stone, suspended like strung bells.
translations.idiomatic: Stone: chime of jade or stone, suspended like bells.

sentences.zh: 絲之屬四：一曰琴，神農制為五弦，周文王加二弦為七者也。

translations.literal: Silk category, four: first, qin—Shennong made five strings; King Wen of Zhou added two for seven.
translations.idiomatic: Silk: qin—Shennong five strings; Zhou Wen seven.

sentences.zh: 二曰瑟，二十七弦，伏犧所作者也。

translations.literal: Second, se—twenty-seven strings, made by Fuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Se—twenty-seven strings by Fuxi.

sentences.zh: 三曰築，十二弦。

translations.literal: Third, zhu—twelve strings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu—twelve strings.

sentences.zh: 四曰箏，十三弦，所謂秦聲，蒙恬所作者也。

translations.literal: Fourth, zheng—thirteen strings, the so-called Qin sound, made by Meng Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng—thirteen strings, Qin sound by Meng Tian.

sentences.zh: 竹之屬三：一曰簫，十六管，長二尺，舜所造者也。

translations.literal: Bamboo category, three: first, xiao—sixteen pipes, two feet long, made by Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo: xiao—sixteen pipes by Shun.

sentences.zh: 二曰篪，長尺四寸，八孔，蘇公所作者也。

translations.literal: Second, chi—one foot four inches long, eight holes, made by Lord Su.
translations.idiomatic: Chi—eight holes by Lord Su.

sentences.zh: 三曰笛，凡十二孔，漢武帝時丘仲所作者也。

translations.literal: Third, di—twelve holes total, made by Qiu Zhong in Emperor Wu of Han's time.
translations.idiomatic: Di—twelve holes by Qiu Zhong under Han Wudi.

sentences.zh: 京房備五音，有七孔，以應七聲。

translations.literal: Jing Fang completed five tones with seven holes to match seven sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang: seven holes for seven sounds.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之笛，長二尺八寸四分四厘有奇，其餘亦上下相次，以為長短。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell di two feet eight inches four fen four li odd; the rest likewise high and low in sequence for length.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell di length set; others sequenced.

sentences.zh: 匏之屬二：一曰笙，二曰竽，並女媧之所作也。

translations.literal: Gourd category, two: first sheng, second yu—both made by Nüwa.
translations.idiomatic: Gourd: sheng and yu by Nüwa.

sentences.zh: 笙列管十九，于匏內施簧而吹之。

translations.literal: Sheng arranges nineteen pipes; reeds placed inside gourd and blown.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng: nineteen pipes with reeds in gourd.

sentences.zh: 竽大，三十六管。

translations.literal: Yu large—thirty-six pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Yu large: thirty-six pipes.

sentences.zh: 土之屬一：曰塤，六孔，暴辛公之所作者也。

translations.literal: Earth category, one: called xun—six holes, made by Duke Bao Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Earth: xun—six holes by Duke Bao Xin.

sentences.zh: 革之屬五：一曰建鼓，夏後氏加四足，謂之足鼓。

translations.literal: Leather category, five: first, set drum—Xia added four feet, called foot drum.
translations.idiomatic: Leather: set drum—Xia foot drum.

sentences.zh: 殷人柱貫之，謂之楹鼓。

translations.literal: Yin people pierced with pillar, called pillar drum.
translations.idiomatic: Yin pillar drum.

sentences.zh: 周人懸之，謂之懸鼓。

translations.literal: Zhou people suspended it, called suspended drum.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou suspended drum.

sentences.zh: 近代相承，植而貫之，謂之建鼓。

translations.literal: Recent ages hand down planting and piercing—called set drum.
translations.idiomatic: Recent ages: planted and pierced set drum.

sentences.zh: 蓋殷所作也。

translations.literal: Likely Yin made it.
translations.idiomatic: Likely Yin invention.

sentences.zh: 又棲翔鷺於其上，不知何代所加。

translations.literal: Also perching flying egrets atop—unknown what age added.
translations.idiomatic: Flying egrets atop—age unknown.

sentences.zh: 或曰，鵠也，取其聲揚而遠聞。

translations.literal: Some say swan, taking sound raised and far heard.
translations.idiomatic: Some say swan—for far-heard sound.

sentences.zh: 或曰，鷺，鼓精也。

translations.literal: Some say egret—drum essence.
translations.idiomatic: Some say egret is drum essence.

sentences.zh: 越王勾踐擊大鼓于雷門以壓吳。

translations.literal: King Goujian of Yue struck great drums at Thunder Gate to overpower Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Goujian struck great drums at Thunder Gate against Wu.

sentences.zh: 晉時移于建康，有雙鷺哾鼓而飛入雲。

translations.literal: Jin times moved to Jiankang; paired egrets cried at drums and flew into clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang: paired egrets cried at drums and flew away.

sentences.zh: 或曰，皆非也。

translations.literal: Some say all are wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Some say all wrong.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「振振鷺，鷺於飛。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Fluttering egrets, egrets in flight."
translations.idiomatic: Odes: "Fluttering egrets in flight."

sentences.zh: 鼓咽咽，醉言歸。

translations.literal: "Drums murmur murmur; drunk words return home."
translations.idiomatic: "Drums murmur; drunk words homeward."

sentences.zh: 」古之君子，悲周道之衰，頌聲之輟，飾鼓以鷺，存其風流。

translations.literal: Ancient gentlemen, grieving Zhou Way's decline and hymn voice's cessation, ornamented drums with egrets, preserving that elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient gentlemen ornamented drums with egrets, preserving elegance.

sentences.zh: 未知孰是。

translations.literal: Unknown which is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Unknown which is correct.

sentences.zh: 靈鼓、靈鞀，併入面。

translations.literal: Spirit drums and spirit hand-drums, together eight faces.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit drums and hand-drums: eight faces.

sentences.zh: 雷鼓、雷鞀，六面。

translations.literal: Thunder drums and thunder hand-drums, six faces.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder drums: six faces.

sentences.zh: 路鼓、路鞀，四面。

translations.literal: Road drums and road hand-drums, four faces.
translations.idiomatic: Road drums: four faces.

sentences.zh: 鼓以桴擊，鞀貫其中而手搖之。

translations.literal: Drums struck with mallet; hand-drums pierced through and shaken by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Drums mallet-struck; hand-drums hand-shaken.

sentences.zh: 又有節鼓，不知誰所造也。

translations.literal: Also beat-keeping drums—unknown who made them.
translations.idiomatic: Beat-keeping drums—maker unknown.

sentences.zh: 木之屬二：一曰柷，如桶，方二尺八寸，中有椎柄，連底動之，令左右擊，以節樂。

translations.literal: Wood category, two: first, zhu—like bucket, square two feet eight inches, mallet handle inside connected to bottom moving it, making left and right strike to beat music.
translations.idiomatic: Wood: zhu—bucket-shaped beat keeper.

sentences.zh: 二曰敔，如伏獸，背有二十七鉏鋙，以竹長尺，橫櫟之，以止樂焉。

translations.literal: Second, yu—like crouching beast, back has twenty-seven notches; bamboo one foot long, struck crosswise to stop music.
translations.idiomatic: Yu—crouching beast back struck to stop music.

sentences.zh: 簨虡，所以懸鐘磬，橫曰簨，飾以鱗屬，植曰虡，飾以臝及羽屬。

translations.literal: Frames are for suspending bells and chimes; horizontal called sun, ornamented with scale creatures; vertical called ju, ornamented with naked and feather creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Frames suspend bells: horizontal sun, vertical ju.

sentences.zh: 簨加木板於上，謂之業。

translations.literal: Sun adds wooden board atop, called ye.
translations.idiomatic: Sun adds board atop—the ye.

sentences.zh: 殷人刻其上為崇牙，以掛懸。

translations.literal: Yin people carved lofty teeth atop for hanging.
translations.idiomatic: Yin carved lofty teeth for hanging.

sentences.zh: 周人畫繒為紵，戴之以璧，垂五采羽於其下，樹於簨虡之角。

translations.literal: Zhou people painted silk as ramie, topped with jade disk, hanging five-color plumes below, planted at frame corners.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou painted silk, jade disk, five-color plumes at corners.

sentences.zh: 近代又加金博山於簨上，垂流蘇，以合采羽。

translations.literal: Recent ages also added gold peaked mountains atop sun, hanging tassels, combining colored plumes.
translations.idiomatic: Recent ages added gold peaks and tassels.

sentences.zh: 五代相因，同用之。

translations.literal: Five dynasties handed down, all used alike.
translations.idiomatic: Five dynasties used alike.

sentences.zh: 始開皇初定令，置《七部樂》：一曰《國伎》，二曰《清商伎》，三曰《高麗伎》，四曰《天竺伎》，五曰《安國伎》，六曰《龜茲伎》，七曰《文康伎》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, regulations fixed, establishing the Seven Department Music: first, State Variety; second, Qing Shang Variety; third, Goguryeo Variety; fourth, Tianzhu Variety; fifth, An Kingdom Variety; sixth, Kucha Variety; seventh, Wenkang Variety.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang established Seven Department Music: State, Qing Shang, Goguryeo, Tianzhu, An, Kucha, Wenkang.

sentences.zh: 又雜有疏勒、扶南、康國、百濟、突厥、新羅、倭國等伎。

translations.literal: Also mixed were Shule, Funan, Kang Kingdom, Baekje, Turkic, Silla, Wa, and other varieties.
translations.idiomatic: Also mixed: Shule, Funan, Kang, Baekje, Turkic, Silla, Wa.

sentences.zh: 其後牛弘請存《鞞》、《鐸》、《巾》、《拂》等四舞，與新伎並陳。

translations.literal: Later Niu Hong requested preserving the four dances Shield, Duo, Scarf, and Whisk, arrayed with new varieties.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong preserved Shield, Duo, Scarf, Whisk dances with new varieties.

sentences.zh: 因稱：「四舞，按漢、魏以來，並施於宴饗。

translations.literal: Thus saying: "The four dances—from Han and Wei onward all deployed at banquets."
translations.idiomatic: Four dances deployed at banquets since Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 《鞞舞》，漢巴、渝舞也。

translations.literal: Shield Dance—Han Ba and Yu dance.
translations.idiomatic: Shield Dance—Han Ba-Yu dance.

sentences.zh: 至章帝造《鞞舞辭》雲'關東有賢女'，魏明代漢曲雲'明明魏皇帝'。

translations.literal: By Emperor Zhang's time Shield Dance lyrics said "east of the pass a worthy woman"; Wei Ming replaced Han melody saying "bright bright Wei emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's Shield lyrics "worthy woman east of pass"; Wei Ming "bright Wei emperor."

sentences.zh: 《鐸舞》，傅玄代魏辭雲'振鐸鳴金'，成公綏賦雲'《鞞鐸》舞庭，八音並陳'是也。

translations.literal: Duo Dance—Fu Xuan replaced Wei lyrics saying "shake duo ring metal"; Cheng Gong Sui's rhapsody says "Shield Duo dance in court, eight sounds all displayed"—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: Duo Dance—Fu Xuan "shake duo ring metal"; Cheng Gong Sui's court description.

sentences.zh: 《拂舞》者，沈約《宋志》云：'吳舞，吳人思晉化。

translations.literal: Whisk Dance—Shen Yue's Song Treatise says: "Wu dance—Wu people thought of Jin transformation."
translations.idiomatic: Whisk Dance—Shen Yue: Wu dance, Wu people thought of Jin.

sentences.zh: '其辭本雲'白符鳩'是也。

translations.literal: Its lyrics originally said "white dove token"—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: Lyrics originally "white dove token."

sentences.zh: 《巾舞》者，《公莫舞》也。

translations.literal: Scarf Dance is the Gongmo Dance.
translations.idiomatic: Scarf Dance is Gongmo Dance.

sentences.zh: 伏滔云：'項莊因舞，欲劍高祖，項伯紆長袖以扞其鋒，魏、晉傳為舞焉。

translations.literal: Fu Tao said: "Xiang Zhuang danced with sword, wished to stab Gaozu; Xiang Bo wrapped long sleeves to block the blade—Wei and Jin transmitted it as dance."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Tao: Xiang Zhuang's sword dance; Xiang Bo's sleeves—transmitted as dance.

sentences.zh: '檢此雖非正樂，亦前代舊聲。

translations.literal: Examining this, though not orthodox music, it is also former-age old sound.
translations.idiomatic: Though not orthodox, it is old sound.

sentences.zh: 故梁武報沈約云：'《鞞》、《鐸》、《巾》、《拂》，古之遺風。

translations.literal: Hence Liang Wu replied to Shen Yue: "Shield, Duo, Scarf, Whisk—ancient surviving winds."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu: Shield, Duo, Scarf, Whisk—ancient winds.

sentences.zh: '楊泓云：'此舞本二八人，桓玄即真，為八佾。

translations.literal: Yang Hong said: "This dance originally two-eight persons; Huan Xuan took the throne, made eight rows."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong: originally sixteen dancers; Huan Xuan made eight rows.

sentences.zh: 後因而不改。

translations.literal: Later thus unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Later unchanged.

sentences.zh: '齊人王僧虔已論其事。

translations.literal: Qi man Wang Sengqian already discussed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengqian discussed it.

sentences.zh: 平陳所得者，猶充八佾，於懸內繼二舞後作之，為失斯大。

translations.literal: What pacifying Chen obtained still filled eight rows; within suspension continuing after the two dances—great error.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's eight-row four dances after the two dances within suspension—great error.

sentences.zh: 檢四舞由來，其實已久。

translations.literal: Examining the four dances' origin, they are actually long established.
translations.idiomatic: Four dances long established.

sentences.zh: 請並在宴會，與雜伎同設，於西涼前奏之。

translations.literal: Please all be at banquets, set with mixed varieties like before, performed before Western Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Please perform four dances at banquets before Western Liang.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「其聲音節奏及舞，悉宜依舊。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Their sound, rhythm, and dance should all follow the old."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor: sound, rhythm, dance follow the old.

sentences.zh: 惟舞人不須捉鞞拂等。

translations.literal: Only dancers need not hold shield and whisk etc.
translations.idiomatic: Only dancers need not hold shield and whisk.

sentences.zh: 」及大業中，煬帝乃定《清樂》、《西涼》、《龜茲》、《天竺》、《康國》、《疏勒》、《安國》、《高麗》、《禮畢》，以為《九部》。

translations.literal: By Daye, Yangdi fixed Clear Music, Western Liang, Kucha, Tianzhu, Kang Kingdom, Shule, An Kingdom, Goguryeo, and Rites Complete as the Nine Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Daye: Yangdi fixed Nine Departments including Clear Music and Rites Complete.

sentences.zh: 樂器工衣創造既成，大備於茲矣。

translations.literal: Instruments, workers, and robes newly made—greatly complete at this point.
translations.idiomatic: Instruments, workers, robes newly made—complete.

sentences.zh: 《清樂》其始即《清商三調》是也，並漢來舊曲。

translations.literal: Clear Music originally is the Clear Shang Three Modes—both Han old pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Clear Music is Clear Shang Three Modes—Han old pieces.

sentences.zh: 樂器形制，並歌章古辭，與魏三祖所作者，皆被於史籍。

translations.literal: Instrument forms and song texts' ancient lyrics, with what Wei's three founders made, are all recorded in histories.
translations.idiomatic: Instrument forms and ancient lyrics recorded in histories.

sentences.zh: 屬晉朝遷播，夷羯竊據，其音分散。

translations.literal: When Jin moved east, barbarians seized territory and its sounds scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Jin moved east; sounds scattered.

sentences.zh: 苻永固平張氏，始於涼州得之。

translations.literal: Fu Yonggu pacified Zhang and first obtained them at Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yonggu obtained them at Liang province.

sentences.zh: 宋武平關中，因而入南，不復存於內地。

translations.literal: Song Wu pacified Guanzhong and thus entered south, no longer kept in inner lands.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wu brought them south, lost in inner lands.

sentences.zh: 及平陳後獲之。

translations.literal: After pacifying Chen they were obtained again.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying Chen recovered them.

sentences.zh: 高祖聽之，善其節奏，曰：「此華夏正聲也。

translations.literal: Gaozu listened and favored their rhythm, saying: "This is Huaxia orthodox sound."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu: "This is Huaxia orthodox sound."

sentences.zh: 昔因永嘉，流于江外，我受天明命，今復會同。

translations.literal: Formerly through Yongjia it flowed beyond the river; I received Heaven's bright mandate—now again united.
translations.idiomatic: Through Yongjia it flowed out; now reunited under mandate.

sentences.zh: 雖賞逐時遷，而古致猶在。

translations.literal: Though appreciation follows time's shift, ancient flavor still remains.
translations.idiomatic: Time shifts; ancient flavor remains.

sentences.zh: 可以此為本，微更損益，去其哀怨，考而補之。

translations.literal: May this be foundation, slightly more increase and decrease, remove grief and resentment, examine and supplement.
translations.idiomatic: Use as foundation; remove grief; examine and supplement.

sentences.zh: 以新定律呂，更造樂器。

translations.literal: With newly fixed pitch law, newly make instruments.
translations.idiomatic: New pitch law; new instruments.

sentences.zh: 」其歌曲有《陽伴》，舞曲有《明君》、《並契》。

translations.literal: Its songs include Yang Companion; dances include Bright Lord and Combined Contract.
translations.idiomatic: Songs: Yang Companion; dances: Bright Lord, Combined Contract.

sentences.zh: 其樂器有鐘、磬、琴、瑟、擊琴、琵琶、箜篌、築、箏、節鼓、笙、笛、簫、篪、塤等十五種，為一部。

translations.literal: Its instruments: bell, chime, qin, se, struck qin, pipa, konghou, zhu, zheng, beat drum, sheng, di, xiao, chi, xun—fifteen kinds, one department.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen instruments including bell, pipa, konghou—one department.

sentences.zh: 工二十五人。

translations.literal: Twenty-five workers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five workers.

sentences.zh: 《西涼》者，起苻氏之末，呂光、沮渠蒙遜等，據有涼州，變龜茲聲為之，號為秦漢伎。

translations.literal: Western Liang began at Fu clan's end; Lü Guang, Juqu Mengxun, and others held Liang province, changing Kucha sound to make it—called Qin-Han variety.
translations.idiomatic: Western Liang: Lü Guang changed Kucha sound—Qin-Han variety.

sentences.zh: 魏太武既平河西得之，謂之《西涼樂》。

translations.literal: Wei Taiwu after pacifying Hexi obtained it—called Western Liang Music.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Taiwu called it Western Liang Music.

sentences.zh: 至魏、周之際，遂謂之《國伎》。

translations.literal: By Wei and Zhou's border it was called State Variety.
translations.idiomatic: Later called State Variety.

sentences.zh: 今曲項琵琶、豎頭箜篌之徒，並出自西域，非華夏舊器。

translations.literal: Now curved-neck pipa, vertical konghou, and such all come from Western Regions—not Huaxia old instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Curved pipa and vertical konghou are Western—not Huaxia old.

sentences.zh: 《楊澤新聲》、《神白馬》之類，生於胡戎。

translations.literal: Yangze New Sound, Spirit White Horse, and such born among barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yangze New Sound and Spirit White Horse born among barbarians.

sentences.zh: 胡戎歌非漢魏遺曲，故其樂器聲調，悉與書史不同。

translations.literal: Barbarian songs are not Han-Wei surviving melodies—hence instrument tones differ from books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian songs differ from Han-Wei and from histories.

sentences.zh: 其歌曲有《永世樂》，解曲有《萬世豐》舞，曲有《于闐佛曲》。

translations.literal: Its songs include Eternal World Music; interlude pieces include Myriad Age Abundance dance; dance pieces include Khotan Buddha Melody.
translations.idiomatic: Songs: Eternal World Music; interludes: Myriad Age Abundance; dance: Khotan Buddha.

sentences.zh: 其樂器有鐘、磬、彈箏、搊箏、臥箜篌、豎箜篌、琵琶、五弦、笙、簫、大篳篥、長笛、小篳篥、橫笛、腰鼓、齊鼓、擔鼓、銅拔、貝等十九種，為一部。

translations.literal: Its instruments: bell, chime, plucked zheng, strummed zheng, horizontal konghou, vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, sheng, xiao, large bili, long di, small bili, transverse di, waist drum, qi drum, shoulder drum, copper cymbal, shell—nineteen kinds, one department.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen instruments including pipa, bili, waist drum—one department.

sentences.zh: 工二十七人。

translations.literal: Twenty-seven workers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven workers.

sentences.zh: 《龜茲》者，起自呂光滅龜茲，因得其聲。

translations.literal: Kucha began when Lü Guang destroyed Kucha and thus obtained its sound.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha: Lü Guang destroyed Kucha and took its sound.

sentences.zh: 呂氏亡，其樂分散，後魏平中原，復獲之。

translations.literal: When Lü clan perished its music scattered; Later Wei pacified Central Plains and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü fell; Later Wei recovered Kucha music.

sentences.zh: 其聲後多變易。

translations.literal: Its sound later much changed.
translations.idiomatic: Its sound later changed much.

sentences.zh: 至隋有《西國龜茲》、《齊朝龜茲》、《土龜茲》等，凡三部。

translations.literal: By Sui there were Western Kingdom Kucha, Qi Dynasty Kucha, and Native Kucha—three departments total.
translations.idiomatic: Sui had three Kucha departments.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，其器大盛於閭幹。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang its instruments greatly flourished in Lügan.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang: instruments flourished in Lügan.

sentences.zh: 時有曹妙達、王長通、李士衡、郭金樂、安進貴等，皆妙絕弦管，新聲奇變，朝改暮易，持其音技，估衒公王之間，舉時爭相慕尚。

translations.literal: At the time Cao Miaoda, Wang Changtong, Li Shiheng, Guo Jinyue, An Jingui, and others—all wondrous in strings and pipes, new sounds strange changes, morning altered evening changed—holding their tonal skill, appraising and displaying among lords and kings; the age competed to admire.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Miaoda and others wondrous in strings—lords competed to admire.

sentences.zh: 高祖病之，謂群臣曰：「聞公等皆好新變，所奏無復正聲，此不祥之大也。

translations.literal: Gaozu was troubled, telling assembled ministers: "Hearing you all favor new changes—the pieces played no longer have orthodox sound. This is greatly inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu troubled: new changes lack orthodox sound—inauguspicious.

sentences.zh: 自家形國，化成人風，勿謂天下方然，公家家自有風俗矣。

translations.literal: "From your own form and state, transforming into human wind—do not say all under Heaven is thus; your families each have their own customs."
translations.idiomatic: Each family has its own customs—not all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 存亡善惡，莫不系之。

translations.literal: "Survival, destruction, good, and evil—none not tied to this."
translations.idiomatic: Survival and good tied to this.

sentences.zh: 樂感人深，事資和雅，公等對親賓宴飲，宜奏正聲；

translations.literal: "Music moves people deeply—affair relies on harmony and elegance; you facing kin and guests at banquets should play orthodox sound;"
translations.idiomatic: Music moves deeply—play orthodox sound before kin and guests.

sentences.zh: 聲不正，何可使兒女聞也！

translations.literal: "sound not orthodox—how may children and daughters hear!"
translations.idiomatic: Non-orthodox sound—how may children hear!

sentences.zh: 」帝雖有此敕，而竟不能救焉。

translations.literal: Though the Emperor had this edict, in the end it could not be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: Edict could not be remedied.

sentences.zh: 煬帝不解音律，略不關懷。

translations.literal: Yangdi did not understand pitch law, barely concerned.
translations.idiomatic: Yangdi ignored pitch law.

sentences.zh: 後大制豔篇，辭極淫綺。

translations.literal: Later he greatly made sensuous pieces—texts extremely licentious and ornate.
translations.idiomatic: Later sensuous licentious pieces.

sentences.zh: 令樂正白明達造新聲，創《萬歲樂》、《藏鉤樂》、《七夕相逢樂》、《投壺樂》、《舞席同心髻》、《玉女行觴》、《神仙留客》、《擲磚續命》、《鬥雞子》、《鬥百草》、《泛龍舟》、《還舊宮》、《長樂花》及《十二時》等曲，掩抑摧藏，哀音斷絕。

translations.literal: Ordered Music Director Bai Mingda to make new sounds, creating Ten Thousand Years Music, Hook-Hiding Music, Qixi Meeting Music, Pitch-Pot Music, Dance Mat Same-Heart Buns, Jade Maiden Passing Cup, Immortals Detaining Guests, Throwing Brick Continuing Life, Cockfighting, Hundred-Plants Contest, Floating Dragon Boat, Returning to Old Palace, Eternal Joy Flower, and Twelve Hours and other pieces—suppressed, hidden, destroyed; mournful voice cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Mingda created licentious pieces—Ten Thousand Years, Floating Dragon Boat, Twelve Hours, etc.

sentences.zh: 帝悅之無已，謂幸臣曰：「多彈曲者，如人多讀書。

translations.literal: The Emperor delighted without end, telling favored ministers: "Many who play pieces are like many who read books."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor: many pieces like many books.

sentences.zh: 讀書多則能撰書，彈曲多即能造曲。

translations.literal: "Many books read then able to compose books; many pieces played then able to make pieces."
translations.idiomatic: Many books enable composing; many pieces enable making.

sentences.zh: 此理之然也。

translations.literal: "This principle is so."
translations.idiomatic: So runs the principle.

sentences.zh: 」因語明達云：「齊氏偏隅，曹妙達猶自封王。

translations.literal: Thus telling Mingda: "Qi was a corner; Cao Miaoda still enfeoffed himself king."
translations.idiomatic: Qi corner—Cao Miaoda still made himself king.

sentences.zh: 我今天下大同，欲貴汝，宜自修謹。

translations.literal: "I today all under Heaven great unity—wish to honor you; should self cultivate and be careful."
translations.idiomatic: Today great unity—I wish to honor you; be careful.

sentences.zh: 」六年，高昌獻《聖明樂》曲，帝令知音者于館所聽之，歸而肄習。

translations.literal: Sixth year, Gaochang presented Holy Bright Music; Emperor ordered those knowing tone to listen at the guest house, return and practice.
translations.idiomatic: Year 6 Gaochang presented Holy Bright Music.

sentences.zh: 及客方獻，先於前奏之，胡夷皆驚焉。

translations.literal: When the guest just presented, first played before them—barbarians all startled.
translations.idiomatic: Played before guests—barbarians startled.

sentences.zh: 其歌曲有《善善摩尼》，解曲有《婆伽兒》，舞曲有《小天》，又有《疏勒鹽》。

translations.literal: Its songs include Good Good Mani; interlude Good Child; dance Little Heaven; also Shule Salt.
translations.idiomatic: Songs: Good Good Mani; interlude Good Child; dance Little Heaven; Shule Salt.

sentences.zh: 其樂器有豎箜篌、琵琶、五弦、笙、笛、簫、篳篥、毛員鼓、都曇鼓、答臘鼓、腰鼓、羯鼓、雞婁鼓、銅拔、貝等十五種，為一部。

translations.literal: Its instruments: vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, sheng, di, xiao, bili, wool member drum, capital dawn drum, answering wax drum, waist drum, jie drum, chicken basket drum, copper cymbal, shell—fifteen kinds, one department.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen Kucha instruments including jie drum, chicken basket drum.

sentences.zh: 工二十人。

translations.literal: Twenty workers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty workers.

sentences.zh: 《天竺》者，起自張重華據有涼州，重四譯來貢男伎，《天竺》即其樂焉。

translations.literal: Tianzhu began when Zhang Chonghua held Liang province; heavy four translations came offering male variety—Tianzhu is that music.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhu: Zhang Chonghua's translations brought male variety.

sentences.zh: 歌曲有《沙石疆》，舞曲有《天曲》。

translations.literal: Songs include Sand Stone Border; dances include Heaven Melody.
translations.idiomatic: Songs: Sand Stone Border; dances: Heaven Melody.

sentences.zh: 樂器有鳳首箜篌、琵琶、五弦、笛、銅鼓、毛員鼓、都曇鼓、銅拔、貝等九種，為一部。

translations.literal: Instruments: phoenix-head konghou, pipa, five-string, di, copper drum, wool member drum, capital dawn drum, copper cymbal, shell—nine kinds, one department.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Tianzhu instruments including phoenix-head konghou.

sentences.zh: 工十二人。

translations.literal: Twelve workers.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve workers.

sentences.zh: 《康國》，起自周武帝娉北狄為後，得其所獲西戎伎，因其聲。

translations.literal: Kang Kingdom began when Zhou Wudi married a Northern Di as consort, obtaining Western Rong variety captured—following its sound.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Kingdom: Zhou Wudi's Di consort brought Western Rong variety.

sentences.zh: 歌曲有《戢殿農和正》，舞曲有《賀蘭缽鼻始》、《末奚波地》、《農惠缽鼻始》、《前拔地惠地》等四曲。

translations.literal: Songs include Ji Palace Farm Harmony Correct; dances include Helan Bowl Nose Start, End Xi Wave Earth, Farm Grace Bowl Nose Start, Front Pull Earth Grace Earth—four pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Kang songs and four dances including Helan Bowl Nose Start.

sentences.zh: 樂器有笛、正鼓、加鼓、銅拔等四種，為一部。

translations.literal: Instruments: di, correct drum, added drum, copper cymbal—four kinds, one department.
translations.idiomatic: Four Kang instruments: di, drums, cymbal.

sentences.zh: 工七人。

translations.literal: Seven workers.
translations.idiomatic: Seven workers.

sentences.zh: 《疏勒》、《安國》、《高麗》，並起自後魏平馮氏及通西域，因得其伎。

translations.literal: Shule, An Kingdom, and Goguryeo all began when Later Wei pacified Lady Feng and opened Western Regions, obtaining their varieties.
translations.idiomatic: Shule, An, Goguryeo from Later Wei and Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 後漸繁會其聲，以別于太樂。

translations.literal: Later gradually rich assembly of their sounds, to distinguish from Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: Later sounds distinguished from Grand Music.

sentences.zh: 《疏勒》，歌曲有《亢利死讓樂》，舞曲有《遠服》，解曲有《鹽曲》。

translations.literal: Shule: songs include Kang Li Death Yield Music; dances include Distant Service; interlude Salt Melody.
translations.idiomatic: Shule: Kang Li Death Yield; dance Distant Service; interlude Salt.

sentences.zh: 樂器有豎箜篌、琵琶、五弦、笛、簫、篳篥、答臘鼓、腰鼓、羯鼓、雞婁鼓等十種，為一部，工十二人。

translations.literal: Instruments: vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, di, xiao, bili, answering wax drum, waist drum, jie drum, chicken basket drum—ten kinds, one department, twelve workers.
translations.idiomatic: Ten Shule instruments, twelve workers.

sentences.zh: 《安國》，歌曲有《附薩單時》，舞曲有《末奚》，解曲有《居和祗》。

translations.literal: An Kingdom: songs include Attached Sa Single Time; dances include End Xi; interlude Ju and Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: An Kingdom: Attached Sa Single Time; dance End Xi.

sentences.zh: 樂器有箜篌、琵琶、五弦、笛、簫、篳篥、雙篳篥、正鼓、和鼓、銅拔等十種，為一部。

translations.literal: Instruments: konghou, pipa, five-string, di, xiao, bili, double bili, correct drum, harmony drum, copper cymbal—ten kinds, one department.
translations.idiomatic: Ten An Kingdom instruments.

sentences.zh: 工十二人。

translations.literal: Twelve workers.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve workers.

sentences.zh: 《高麗》，歌曲有《芝棲》，舞曲有《歌芝棲》。

translations.literal: Goguryeo: songs include Zhi Qi; dances include Song Zhi Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo: Zhi Qi; dance Song Zhi Qi.

sentences.zh: 樂器有彈箏、臥箜篌、豎箜篌、琵琶、五弦、笛、笙、簫、小篳篥、桃皮篳篥、腰鼓、齊鼓、擔鼓、貝等十四種，為一部。

translations.literal: Instruments: plucked zheng, horizontal konghou, vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, di, sheng, xiao, small bili, peach-skin bili, waist drum, qi drum, shoulder drum, shell—fourteen kinds, one department.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen Goguryeo instruments.

sentences.zh: 工十八人。

translations.literal: Eighteen workers.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen workers.

sentences.zh: 《禮畢》者，本出自晉太尉庾亮家。

translations.literal: Rites Complete originally came from Jin Grand Marshal Yu Liang's house.
translations.idiomatic: Rites Complete from Jin Marshal Yu Liang's house.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，其伎追思亮，因假為其面，執翳以舞，象其容，取其諡以號之，謂之為《文康樂》。

translations.literal: When Liang died, his variety mourned Liang; thus borrowing his face, holding feather fans to dance, imitating his appearance, taking his posthumous title to name it—called Cultured Peace Music.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang's performers mourned him as Cultured Peace Music.

sentences.zh: 每奏九部樂終則陳之，故以禮畢為名。

translations.literal: Each time the nine departments' music ended it was performed—hence named Rites Complete.
translations.idiomatic: Performed after nine departments—Rites Complete.

sentences.zh: 其行曲有《單交路》，舞曲有《散花》。

translations.literal: Its processional pieces include Single Crossroad; dances include Scattering Flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Processional Single Crossroad; dance Scattering Flowers.

sentences.zh: 樂器有笛、笙、簫、篪、鈴槃、鞞、腰鼓等七種，三懸為一部。

translations.literal: Instruments: di, sheng, xiao, chi, bell tray, shield, waist drum—seven kinds, triple suspension one department.
translations.idiomatic: Seven instruments, triple suspension.

sentences.zh: 工二十二人。

translations.literal: Twenty-two workers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two workers.

sentences.zh: 始齊武平中，有魚龍爛漫、俳優、硃儒、山車、巨象、拔井、種瓜、殺馬、剝驢等，奇怪異端，百有餘物，名為百戲。

translations.literal: At the beginning in Qi Wuping, there were dragon-and-fish splendor, actors, cinnabar Confucians, mountain carts, great elephants, well-pulling, melon-planting, horse-killing, donkey-flaying, and more—strange exotic tricks, over one hundred items, called Hundred Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wuping Hundred Entertainments: dragons, elephants, well-pulling, over one hundred tricks.

sentences.zh: 周時，鄭譯有寵于宣帝，奏征齊散樂人，並會京師為之。

translations.literal: In Zhou's time, Zheng Yi had favor with Emperor Xuan; memorialized gathering Qi scattered musicians, all meeting at the capital for this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou: Zheng Yi gathered Qi scattered musicians at capital.

sentences.zh: 蓋秦角抵之流者也。

translations.literal: Likely the stream of Qin horn-butting.
translations.idiomatic: Likely Qin horn-butting tradition.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，並放遣之。

translations.literal: At Kaihuang beginning, all released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang beginning: all released.

sentences.zh: 及大業二年，突厥染幹來朝，煬帝欲誇之，總追四方散樂，大集東都。

translations.literal: By Daye second year, Turkic Yiran Khan came to court; Yangdi wished to display grandeur—totally recalled scattered musicians from four directions, greatly gathering at Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Daye 2: Yangdi recalled scattered musicians to impress Turks.

sentences.zh: 初于芳華苑積翠池側，帝帷宮女觀之。

translations.literal: First at Accumulated Emerald Pool beside Fragrant Garden—Emperor curtained palace women to watch.
translations.idiomatic: First at Accumulated Emerald Pool—palace women watched.

sentences.zh: 有舍利先來，戲於場內，須臾跳躍，激水滿衢，黿鼉龜鰲，水人蟲魚，遍覆於地。

translations.literal: There was a relic first coming, playing in the field; in a moment leaping, splashing water filling streets—turtles, crocodiles, turtles, fish, water people, insects, and fish all covering the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Relic leaped; water filled streets with creatures.

sentences.zh: 又有大鯨魚，噴霧翳日，倏忽化成黃龍，長七八丈，聳踴而出，名曰《黃龍變》。

translations.literal: Also a great whale spouting mist hiding the sun; suddenly transforming into yellow dragon, seven or eight zhang long, soaring out—named Yellow Dragon Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Great whale became yellow dragon—Yellow Dragon Transformation.

sentences.zh: 又以繩系兩柱，相去十丈，遣二倡女對舞繩上，相逢切肩而過，歌舞不輟。

translations.literal: Also rope tied two pillars ten zhang apart; sent two singing girls dancing on rope, meeting shoulder to shoulder passing—singing and dancing unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Two girls danced on rope between pillars.

sentences.zh: 又為夏育扛鼎，取車輪石臼大甕器等，各於掌上而跳弄之。

translations.literal: Also made Xia Yu carrying tripod; taking cart wheel, stone mortar, great urn vessels and such, each juggling on palm.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yu carrying tripod; juggling wheels and urns on palms.

sentences.zh: 並二人戴竿，其上有舞，忽然騰透而換易之。

translations.literal: Also two persons wearing poles; atop them dancing, suddenly soaring through and exchanging.
translations.idiomatic: Two pole-dancers exchanged mid-air.

sentences.zh: 又有神鰲負山，幻人吐火，千變萬化，曠古莫儔。

translations.literal: Also spirit turtle bearing mountain, illusionists spitting fire—thousand changes ten thousand transformations, antiquity unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit turtle bearing mountain; fire-spitting illusionists.

sentences.zh: 染幹大駭之。

translations.literal: Yiran greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yiran greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 自是皆于太常教習。

translations.literal: From then all taught at the Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: From then taught at Grand Music Master.

sentences.zh: 每歲正月，萬國來朝，留至十五日，於端門外，建國門內，綿亙八里，列為戲場。

translations.literal: Each year first month, ten thousand states come to court, staying until fifteenth day; outside Duan Gate, inside Jianguo Gate, stretching eight li, arrayed as entertainment ground.
translations.idiomatic: New Year: eight-li entertainment ground outside Duan Gate.

sentences.zh: 百官起棚夾路，從昏達旦，以縱觀之。

translations.literal: Hundred officials raised sheds flanking the road—from dusk to dawn, to watch freely.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' sheds from dusk to dawn.

sentences.zh: 至晦而罷。

translations.literal: Until month's end then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Until month's end.

sentences.zh: 伎人皆衣錦繡繒彩。

translations.literal: Entertainers all wore brocade silk colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: Entertainers wore brocade and silk.

sentences.zh: 其歌舞者，多為婦人服，鳴環佩，飾以花毦者，殆三萬人。

translations.literal: Those singing and dancing mostly wore women's dress, ringing pendants, ornamented with flowery tufts—nearly thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly thirty thousand singers in women's dress.

sentences.zh: 初課京兆、河南制此衣服，而兩京繒錦，為之中虛。

translations.literal: Initially assessed Jingzhao and Henan to make these clothes—both capitals' silk brocade emptied thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao and Henan silk brocade emptied.

sentences.zh: 三年，駕幸榆林，突厥啟民朝於行宮，帝又設以示之。

translations.literal: Third year, imperial progress to Yulin; Turkic Qimin attended at traveling palace—Emperor again set display to show him.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3 Yulin: display for Qimin.

sentences.zh: 六年，諸夷大獻方物。

translations.literal: Sixth year, all barbarians greatly presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: Year 6: barbarians presented products.

sentences.zh: 突厥啟民以下，皆國主親來朝賀。

translations.literal: From Turkic Qimin downward, all state lords personally came to court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: State lords personally congratulated.

sentences.zh: 乃于天津街盛陳百戲，自海內凡有奇伎，無不總萃。

translations.literal: Then at Tianjin Street grandly arrayed Hundred Entertainments—within the seas whatever strange skills, none not all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin Street Hundred Entertainments—all strange skills gathered.

sentences.zh: 崇侈器玩，盛飾衣服，皆用珠翠金銀，錦罽絺繡。

translations.literal: Honoring extravagant vessels and playthings, richly ornamenting clothes—all using pearl, jade, gold, silver, brocade, fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant vessels; pearl, jade, gold, brocade clothes.

sentences.zh: 其營費钜億萬。

translations.literal: Operating expenses tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Expenses tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 關西以安德王雄總之，東都以齊王暕總之，金石匏革之聲，聞數十里外。

translations.literal: Guanxi under Prince of Ande Xiong supervised; Eastern Capital under Prince of Qi Yang supervised—metal, stone, gourd, leather sounds heard several tens of li away.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Xiong and Yang supervised—music heard tens of li.

sentences.zh: 彈弦扌厭管以上，一萬八千人。

translations.literal: Plucked strings and pressed pipes and above—eighteen thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen thousand string and pipe performers.

sentences.zh: 大列炬火，光燭天地，百戲之盛，振古無比。

translations.literal: Greatly arraying torch fire, light illuminating Heaven and Earth—Hundred Entertainments' splendor, shaking antiquity without compare.
translations.idiomatic: Torch fire illuminated Heaven and Earth—unmatched splendor.

sentences.zh: 自是每年以為常焉。

translations.literal: From then annually made constant.
translations.idiomatic: Annual thereafter.

sentences.zh: 故事，天子有事于太廟，備法駕，陳羽葆，以入於次。

translations.literal: Precedent: when Son of Heaven has affair at Grand Temple, full imperial carriage prepared, feather canopy displayed, to enter the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent: Grand Temple affair uses full carriage and feather canopy.

sentences.zh: 禮畢升車，而鼓吹並作。

translations.literal: Rites complete ascending carriage—wind-and-drum all together perform.
translations.idiomatic: Rites complete—wind-and-drum perform on ascending carriage.

sentences.zh: 開皇十七年詔曰：「昔五帝異樂，三王殊禮，皆隨事而有損益，因情而立節文。

translations.literal: Kaihuang seventeenth year edict: "Formerly Five Thearchs different music, Three Kings different rites—all follow affairs with increase and decrease, establish protocol according to feeling."
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 17: Five Thearchs different music; rites follow affairs.

sentences.zh: 仰惟祭享宗廟，瞻敬如在，罔極之感，情深茲日。

translations.literal: "Looking up considering sacrificial offering to ancestral temple, gazing reverence as if present, boundless feeling, feeling deep on this day."
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral sacrifice—gazing as if present; feeling deep today.

sentences.zh: 而禮畢升路，鼓吹發音，還入宮門，金石振響。

translations.literal: "Yet rites complete ascending road, wind-and-drum sound forth; returning entering palace gate, metal and stone shake sound."
translations.idiomatic: Yet rites complete then wind-and-drum—sorrow and joy same day.

sentences.zh: 斯則哀樂同日，心事相違，情所不安，理實未允。

translations.literal: "This then sorrow and joy same day, heart affair mutually opposed, feeling place not settled, principle actually not permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Sorrow and joy same day—heart opposed; principle not permitted.

sentences.zh: 宜改茲往式，用弘禮教。

translations.literal: "Should change this former form, use to expand ritual teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Change former form; expand ritual teaching.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，享廟日不須設鼓吹，殿庭勿設樂懸。

translations.literal: "From now after, temple feast day need not set wind-and-drum; hall court do not set music suspension."
translations.idiomatic: Temple feast day: no wind-and-drum; hall no suspension.

sentences.zh: 在廟內及諸祭，並依舊。

translations.literal: "Within temple and all sacrifices still follow old."
translations.idiomatic: Within temple and sacrifices follow old.

sentences.zh: 其王公已下，祭私廟日，不得作音樂。

translations.literal: "Princes and dukes downward, private temple sacrifice day, may not make music."
translations.idiomatic: Princes' private temple sacrifice: no music.
Closing quote of edict.

sentences.zh: 至大業中，煬帝制宴饗設鼓吹，依梁為十二案。

translations.literal: By Daye, Yangdi regulated banquet setting wind-and-drum—following Liang as twelve stands.
translations.idiomatic: Daye: Yangdi banquet wind-and-drum—twelve stands like Liang.

sentences.zh: 案別有錞於、鉦、鐸、軍樂鼓吹等一部。

translations.literal: Each stand separately has chunyu, cymbal, duo, army music wind-and-drum and such one department.
translations.idiomatic: Each stand: chunyu, cymbal, duo, army wind-and-drum.

sentences.zh: 案下皆熊罷貙豹，騰倚承之，以象百獸之舞。

translations.literal: Below stands all bear, leopard, and lynx lean and support—to image the dance of a hundred beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Below stands bear and leopard—to image beasts' dance.

sentences.zh: 其大駕鼓吹，並硃漆畫。

translations.literal: Grand carriage wind-and-drum all cinnabar lacquer painted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand carriage wind-and-drum cinnabar lacquer.

sentences.zh: 大駕鼓吹、小鼓加金鐲、羽葆鼓、鐃鼓、節鼓，皆五采重蓋，其羽葆鼓，仍飾以羽葆。

translations.literal: Grand carriage wind-and-drum, small drums adding gold duo, feather-canopy drums, nao drums, beat drums—all five-color layered canopy; feather-canopy drums still ornamented with feather canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand wind-and-drum: five-color canopies; feather-canopy drums.

sentences.zh: 長鳴、中鳴、大小橫吹，五采衣幡，緋掌，畫交龍，五采腳。

translations.literal: Long whistle, middle whistle, large and small transverse blow—five-color cloth banners, crimson palms, painted intertwined dragons, five-color feet.
translations.idiomatic: Long and transverse blow: five-color banners, dragon-painted.

sentences.zh: 大角幡亦如之。

translations.literal: Great horn banners likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Great horn banners likewise.

sentences.zh: 大鼓、長鳴、大橫吹、節鼓及橫吹後笛、簫、篳篥、笳、桃皮篳篥等工人服，皆緋地苣文為袍袴及帽。

translations.literal: Great drums, long whistle, great transverse blow, beat drums and transverse blow rear di, xiao, bili, horn, peach-skin bili and such workers' dress—all crimson ground ju-pattern robes, trousers, and caps.
translations.idiomatic: Great drums and transverse blow workers: crimson ju-pattern robes.

sentences.zh: 金鉦、㭎鼓，其鉦鼓皆加八角紫傘。

translations.literal: Metal cymbal, gang drum—its cymbal drums all add eight-corner purple umbrellas.
translations.idiomatic: Metal cymbal and gang drum: eight-corner purple umbrellas.

sentences.zh: 小鼓、中鳴、小橫吹及橫吹後笛、簫、篳篥、笳、桃皮篳篥等工人服，並青地苣文袍袴及帽。

translations.literal: Small drums, middle whistle, small transverse blow and transverse blow rear di, xiao, bili, horn, peach-skin bili workers' dress—all blue ground ju-pattern robes, trousers, and caps.
translations.idiomatic: Small drums and pipes: blue ju-pattern robes.

sentences.zh: 羽葆鼓、鐃及歌、簫、笳工人服，並武弁，硃褠衣，革帶。

translations.literal: Feather-canopy drums, nao and song, xiao, horn workers' dress—all martial caps, cinnabar-trimmed robes, leather belts.
translations.idiomatic: Feather-canopy and song workers: martial caps, cinnabar trim.

sentences.zh: 大角工人，平巾幘，緋衫，白布大口袴。

translations.literal: Great horn workers: plain kerchief, crimson shirt, white cloth large trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Great horn workers: plain kerchief, crimson shirt.

sentences.zh: 其鼓吹督帥服，與大角同。

translations.literal: Wind-and-drum supervising commanders' dress same as great horn.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising commanders dress as great horn.

sentences.zh: 以下准督帥服，亦如之。

translations.literal: Below following supervising commanders' dress, also likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Below commanders likewise.

sentences.zh: 㭎鼓一曲，十二變，與金鉦同。

translations.literal: Gang drum one piece, twelve changes, same as metal cymbal.
translations.idiomatic: Gang drum: twelve changes as metal cymbal.

sentences.zh: 夜警用一曲俱盡。

translations.literal: Night watch uses one piece all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Night watch: one piece exhausted.

sentences.zh: 次奏大鼓。

translations.literal: Next play great drum.
translations.idiomatic: Next: great drum.

sentences.zh: 大鼓，一十五曲供大駕，一十二曲供皇太子，一十曲供王公等。

translations.literal: Great drum: fifteen pieces for grand carriage, twelve for crown prince, ten for princes and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Great drum: 15 grand carriage, 12 crown prince, 10 princes.

sentences.zh: 小鼓，九曲供大駕，三曲供皇太子及王公等。

translations.literal: Small drum: nine pieces for grand carriage, three for crown prince and princes.
translations.idiomatic: Small drum: 9 grand carriage, 3 crown prince and princes.

sentences.zh: 長鳴色角，一百二十具供大駕，三十六具供皇太子，十八具供王公等。

translations.literal: Long whistle color horn: one hundred twenty for grand carriage, thirty-six crown prince, eighteen princes.
translations.idiomatic: Long whistle horn: 120 grand carriage, 36 crown prince, 18 princes.

sentences.zh: 次鳴色角，一百二十具供大駕，十二具供皇太子，一十具供王公等。

translations.literal: Next whistle color horn: one hundred twenty grand carriage, twelve crown prince, ten princes.
translations.idiomatic: Next whistle horn: 120 grand carriage, 12 crown prince, 10 princes.

sentences.zh: 大角，第一曲起捉馬，第二曲被馬，第三曲騎馬，第四曲行，第五曲入陣，第六曲收軍，第七曲下營。

translations.literal: Great horn: first piece begins Seizing Horse, second Treading Horse, third Riding Horse, fourth Marching, fifth Entering Battle, sixth Withdrawing Army, seventh Leaving Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Great horn seven pieces: Seizing Horse through Leaving Camp.

sentences.zh: 皆以三通為一曲。

translations.literal: All take three signals as one piece.
translations.idiomatic: Three signals per piece.

sentences.zh: 其辭並本之鮮卑。

translations.literal: Their lyrics all derive from Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Lyrics derive from Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 鐃鼓，十二曲供大駕，六曲供皇太子，三曲供王公等。

translations.literal: Nao drum: twelve pieces grand carriage, six crown prince, three princes.
translations.idiomatic: Nao drum: 12 grand carriage, 6 crown prince, 3 princes.

sentences.zh: 其樂器有鼓，並歌簫、笳。

translations.literal: Its instruments have drums, and song xiao and horn.
translations.idiomatic: Instruments: drums, song xiao, horn.

sentences.zh: 大橫吹，二十九曲供大駕，九曲供皇太子，七曲供王公。

translations.literal: Great transverse blow: twenty-nine pieces grand carriage, nine crown prince, seven princes.
translations.idiomatic: Great transverse blow: 29 grand carriage, 9 crown prince, 7 princes.

sentences.zh: 其樂器有角、節鼓、笛、簫、篳篥、笳、桃皮篳篥。

translations.literal: Its instruments have horn, beat drum, di, xiao, bili, horn, peach-skin bili.
translations.idiomatic: Instruments: horn, beat drum, di, xiao, bili, horn, peach-skin bili.

sentences.zh: 小橫吹，十二曲供大駕，夜警則十二曲俱用。

translations.literal: Small transverse blow: twelve pieces grand carriage; night watch then twelve pieces all used.
translations.idiomatic: Small transverse blow: 12 grand carriage; night watch all 12.

sentences.zh: 其樂器有角、笛、簫、篳篥、笳、桃皮篳篥。

translations.literal: Its instruments have horn, di, xiao, bili, horn, peach-skin bili.
translations.idiomatic: Instruments: horn, di, xiao, bili, horn, peach-skin bili.
